literature.headline_zh: 人乳头瘤病毒本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期人乳头瘤病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 综述得出的结论是,HPV16 E2是病毒生命周期中的关键调节蛋白,在DNA复制和基因表达中发挥着核心作用。还值得注意的是,HPV16 E2在低分化宫颈病变细胞中高表达,可能通过抑制E6和E7癌基因来抑制肿瘤形成。 [10.1007/s11033-026-12813-8]
完成 HPV 疫苗接种 系列的青少年比例为 26.3%(95% 置信区间,23.3-29.3)。与完整的 疫苗接种 呈正相关的因素包括母亲受过中等或以上教育、母亲共同或自主决策、之前的 宫颈癌 筛查以及对 HPV 的良好了解。相反,高信息超载和决策疲劳与完成 疫苗接种 时间表的较低几率相关。 [10.4082/kjfm.26.0105]

该研究鉴定出 6,462 个体细胞 突变 富含癌症相关通路,特别是 PI3K-Akt 信号传导。PIK3CA 是最常发生突变的基因 (42%),其频率显着高于 HPV16 阳性 TCGA-CESC 肿瘤 (26.21%) (p < 0.04)。与 TCGA-CESC 不同,印度 PIK3CA 突变肿瘤富含晚期疾病。与 PIK3CA 野生肿瘤相比,这些肿瘤表现出较低的病毒载量、较高的肿瘤 突变 负荷和更具侵袭性的分子表型。基于 CIBERSORT 的免疫分析显示,PIK3CA 突变肿瘤和正常组织之间的免疫细胞浸润(包括 CD8+ T 细胞)相当,而 PIK3CA 野生肿瘤与正常组织相比,浸润显着增强。 [10.64898/2026.10.27.26366457]

key_findings_en: The review concludes that HPV16 E2 is a key regulatory protein in the viral life cycle, playing a central role in DNA replication and gene expression. The proportion of adolescents who completed the HPV vaccination series was 26.3% (95% confidence interval, 23.3-29.3). [10.4082/kjfm.26.0105]

The study identified 6,462 somatic mutations enriched in cancer-related pathways, particularly PI3K-Akt signaling. PIK3CA was the most recurrently mutated gene (42%), significantly higher frequency (p < 0.04) than in HPV16-positive TCGA-CESC tumors (26.21%). [10.64898/2026.10.27.26366457]

news.headline_zh: 人乳头瘤病毒本期公共卫生新闻动态
news.lead_zh: 本期人乳头瘤病毒新闻集中呈现以下动态。
key_findings_zh: 一项横断面研究发现,在无症状的乌干达农村妇女中,患病率 (hrHPV) 的 患病率 检测结果呈高水平,其中 25.3% 的检测结果呈阳性。研究还指出,HPV16 和 HPV18 群体之外的感染很常见,并且 hrHPV 基因型与 VIA 结果之间没有发现统计学上的显着关系。 [news-cfa4cd86e5fc82c0]
一项回顾性研究发现,在进行高级别宫颈细胞学检查的女性中,HPV16与最高的癌症风险相关,HPV16阳性个体显示癌前病变和浸润性鳞状细胞癌的比例最高。 [news-5a633b8620f25ca0]
一项研究发现,分子 HPV 检测可以识别子宫颈抹片检查漏掉的宫颈异常情况。内容中报道了这项研究,但没有确认具体的实体或事件。 [news-975827f3854dcf5f]
所提供的证据没有用经过验证的英语清楚地报告中心事件。 [news-75724e885f2407a7]

A cross-sectional study identified a high prevalence of high-risk HPV (hrHPV) among asymptomatic rural Ugandan women, with 25.3% testing positive. [news-cfa4cd86e5fc82c0]. A retrospective study found that HPV16 is associated with the highest cancer risk among women with high-grade cervical cytology, with HPV16-positive individuals showing the highest proportions of precancerous lesions and invasive squamous cell carcinoma. A study found that molecular HPV testing can identify cervical abnormalities missed by Pap smears. The study is reported in the content, but no specific entity or event is confirmed. [news-975827f3854dcf5f]. The supplied evidence does not clearly report the central event in verified English. [news-75724e885f2407a7].

papers.title: Completion of human papillomavirus vaccination and its determinants among adolescents in Southern Ethiopia: a convergent parallel mixed-methods study.
papers.abstract: Background: Cervical cancer is the second most common cancer among women in Ethiopia and is primarily attributable to human papillomavirus (HPV) infection. Although HPV vaccination has been introduced, completion of the recommended two-dose schedule remains suboptimal. Existing evidence has largely focused on access and awareness, with limited attention to cognitive, sociocultural, and maternal decision-making factors influencing completion. This study assessed the magnitude and determinants of second-dose or complete HPV vaccination among adolescents in southern Ethiopia using a mixed-methods approach. Methods: A community-based cross-sectional survey was conducted among 832 mothers of adolescent girls aged 9-14 years, selected using a multistage sampling method. Data were collected using a semi-structured questionnaire and analyzed with IBM SPSS ver. A binary logistic regression model was used to identify factors associated with vaccine completion. Additionally, in-depth interviews were conducted with 12 purposively selected mothers and analyzed thematically to explore perceptions influencing vaccine completion. Results: The proportion of adolescents who completed the HPV vaccination series was 26.3% (95% confidence interval, 23.3-29.3). Factors positively associated with complete vaccination included maternal education at the secondary or higher, shared or autonomous maternal decision-making, prior cervical cancer screening and good knowledge of HPV. Conversely, high information overload and decision fatigue were associated with lower odds of completing the vaccination schedule. Qualitative findings revealed that mothers' decisions were shaped by cultural beliefs, trust in health workers, peer and social media influences, and prior healthcare experience. Conclusion: HPV vaccination completion was low and was associated with interacting cognitive, socio-cultural, and health-system factors. Interventions should move beyond awareness creation to address information burden, strengthen maternal decision-making autonomy, and improve trust through consistent counseling.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the completion of the human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination series among adolescents in southern Ethiopia, focusing on the factors influencing vaccine uptake. The research highlights that despite HPV vaccination being introduced, completion rates remain suboptimal. The study employs a mixed-methods approach, combining a community-based cross-sectional survey with in-depth interviews to explore both quantitative and qualitative determinants of vaccine completion. Results show that only 26.3% of adolescents completed the HPV vaccination series, with maternal education, decision-making autonomy, and knowledge of HPV being positively associated with completion. Conversely, high information overload and decision fatigue were linked to lower completion rates. Qualitative insights reveal that cultural beliefs, trust in health workers, and social influences significantly shape mothers' decisions. The authors interpret these findings as indicating that interventions should address information burden and enhance maternal autonomy to improve vaccination rates. The study's implications suggest a need for targeted strategies in public health to increase HPV vaccine completion, while its limitations include the cross-sectional design and potential recall bias in self-reported data.

papers.title_zh: 完成埃塞俄比亚南部青少年的 人乳头瘤病毒 疫苗接种 及其决定因素:一项收敛平行混合方法研究。
papers.source_body_en: Background: Cervical cancer is the second most common cancer among women in Ethiopia and is primarily attributable to human papillomavirus (HPV) infection. Although HPV vaccination has been introduced, completion of the recommended two-dose schedule remains suboptimal. Existing evidence has largely focused on access and awareness, with limited attention to cognitive, sociocultural, and maternal decision-making factors influencing completion. This study assessed the magnitude and determinants of second-dose or complete HPV vaccination among adolescents in southern Ethiopia using a mixed-methods approach. Methods: A community-based cross-sectional survey was conducted among 832 mothers of adolescent girls aged 9-14 years, selected using a multistage sampling method. Data were collected using a semi-structured questionnaire and analyzed with IBM SPSS ver. A binary logistic regression model was used to identify factors associated with vaccine completion. Additionally, in-depth interviews were conducted with 12 purposively selected mothers and analyzed thematically to explore perceptions influencing vaccine completion. Results: The proportion of adolescents who completed the HPV vaccination series was 26.3% (95% confidence interval, 23.3-29.3). Factors positively associated with complete vaccination included maternal education at the secondary or higher, shared or autonomous maternal decision-making, prior cervical cancer screening and good knowledge of HPV. Conversely, high information overload and decision fatigue were associated with lower odds of completing the vaccination schedule. Qualitative findings revealed that mothers' decisions were shaped by cultural beliefs, trust in health workers, peer and social media influences, and prior healthcare experience. Conclusion: HPV vaccination completion was low and was associated with interacting cognitive, socio-cultural, and health-system factors. Interventions should move beyond awareness creation to address information burden, strengthen maternal decision-making autonomy, and improve trust through consistent counseling.

papers.title: Multifaceted HPV16 E2 as a potential therapeutic target for cervical cancer and beyond
papers.abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV) can cause a variety of epithelial lesions, including the malignant proliferation of host cells and even cervical cancer. HPV E2 can play an important role in regulating viral gene expression, viral replication and transcription, and also can participate in the isolation of viral genome during cell division. HPV16 E2 protein is highly expressed in low-differentiated cervical lesion cells, but decreased or disappeared with the increase of cervical lesion grade. As both the initiation protein for DNA replication and the major transcriptional regulator for HPV16 gene expression, E2 protein may play a key role in the viral life cycle. HPV16 E2 protein as a sequence specific DNA binding protein, can bind with the specific DNA recognition sequence on the promoters of E6 and E7 oncogenes, and then inhibit the transcription and expression of E6 and E7 oncogenes, thus inducing cell apoptosis and suppressing tumor formation. Therefore, therapeutic strategies aimed at restoring or enhancing HPV16 E2 function may hold promise for the prevention and treatment of HPV-related cancers, including (i) gene-therapy-mediated E2 restoration; (ii) direct delivery of E2 protein; (iii) E2 stabilization through modulation of interacting pathways (e.g., TopBP1, Brd4); and (iv) E2-based therapeutic vaccines. These approaches may exert antitumor effects by repressing E6/E7 oncogenes, regulating the cell cycle, inhibiting cell proliferation, and inducing apoptosis.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on Human papillomaviruses (HPV), specifically HPV16, and its role in cervical cancer and other HPV-associated malignancies. The central question is whether HPV16 E2 can serve as a therapeutic target for the prevention and treatment of these diseases.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a narrative analysis of the biological functions of HPV16 E2. It does not report on systematic review methods, databases, or meta-analysis. The evidence is derived from general descriptions of HPV16 E2's role in viral replication, transcription, and oncogenesis.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that HPV16 E2 is a key regulatory protein in the viral life cycle, playing a central role in DNA replication and gene expression. It is also noted that HPV16 E2 is highly expressed in low-differentiated cervical lesion cells and may suppress tumor formation by inhibiting E6 and E7 oncogenes.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review highlights that the expression of HPV16 E2 decreases with increasing cervical lesion grade, but it does not provide evidence on the mechanisms behind this change or its clinical implications. There is no mention of conflicting findings or evidence gaps related to the therapeutic potential of E2.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review suggests that therapeutic strategies targeting HPV16 E2, such as gene therapy, protein delivery, pathway modulation, and vaccines, may offer promising avenues for the prevention and treatment of HPV-related cancers. These approaches could potentially repress E6/E7 oncogenes, regulate the cell cycle, inhibit proliferation, and induce apoptosis.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the potential of HPV16 E2 as a therapeutic target for cervical cancer and other HPV-associated malignancies. It highlights the protein's role in regulating viral gene expression, replication, and transcription, as well as its ability to bind to specific DNA sequences and inhibit oncogenes like E6 and E7. The review suggests that restoring or enhancing E2 function through various strategies could suppress tumor formation and induce apoptosis. While the evidence is primarily descriptive, it outlines possible therapeutic interventions, including gene therapy, protein delivery, pathway modulation, and vaccines. The review does not address controversies or evidence gaps directly, but it emphasizes the need for further research into E2-based therapies for HPV-related cancers.

elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 综述得出的结论是,HPV16 E2是病毒生命周期中的关键调节蛋白,在DNA复制和基因表达中发挥着核心作用。还值得注意的是,HPV16 E2在低分化宫颈病变细胞中高表达,可能通过抑制E6和E7癌基因来抑制肿瘤形成。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该综述强调,HPV16 E2 的表达随着宫颈病变级别的增加而降低,但没有提供这种变化背后的机制或其临床意义的证据。没有提及与 E2 治疗潜力相关的相互矛盾的发现或证据差距。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 该综述表明,针对 HPV16 E2 的治疗策略,例如基因治疗、蛋白质递送、通路调节和 疫苗,可能为 HPV 相关癌症的预防和 治疗 提供有希望的途径。这些方法可能会抑制 E6/E7 癌基因、调节细胞周期、抑制增殖并诱导细胞凋亡。

analysis_en.scope_and_question: The review focuses on Human papillomaviruses (HPV), specifically HPV16, and its role in cervical cancer and other HPV-associated malignancies. The central question is whether HPV16 E2 can serve as a therapeutic target for the prevention and treatment of these diseases.
analysis_en.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a narrative analysis of the biological functions of HPV16 E2. It does not report on systematic review methods, databases, or meta-analysis. The evidence is derived from general descriptions of HPV16 E2's role in viral replication, transcription, and oncogenesis.
analysis_en.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that HPV16 E2 is a key regulatory protein in the viral life cycle, playing a central role in DNA replication and gene expression. It is also noted that HPV16 E2 is highly expressed in low-differentiated cervical lesion cells and may suppress tumor formation by inhibiting E6 and E7 oncogenes.
analysis_en.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review highlights that the expression of HPV16 E2 decreases with increasing cervical lesion grade, but it does not provide evidence on the mechanisms behind this change or its clinical implications. There is no mention of conflicting findings or evidence gaps related to the therapeutic potential of E2.
analysis_en.research_and_practice_implications: The review suggests that therapeutic strategies targeting HPV16 E2, such as gene therapy, protein delivery, pathway modulation, and vaccines, may offer promising avenues for the prevention and treatment of HPV-related cancers. These approaches could potentially repress E6/E7 oncogenes, regulate the cell cycle, inhibit proliferation, and induce apoptosis.

papers.title_zh: 多方面的 HPV16 E2 作为 宫颈癌 及其他药物的潜在治疗靶点
papers.source_body_en: Human papillomavirus (HPV) can cause a variety of epithelial lesions, including the malignant proliferation of host cells and even cervical cancer. HPV E2 can play an important role in regulating viral gene expression, viral replication and transcription, and also can participate in the isolation of viral genome during cell division. HPV16 E2 protein is highly expressed in low-differentiated cervical lesion cells, but decreased or disappeared with the increase of cervical lesion grade. As both the initiation protein for DNA replication and the major transcriptional regulator for HPV16 gene expression, E2 protein may play a key role in the viral life cycle. HPV16 E2 protein as a sequence specific DNA binding protein, can bind with the specific DNA recognition sequence on the promoters of E6 and E7 oncogenes, and then inhibit the transcription and expression of E6 and E7 oncogenes, thus inducing cell apoptosis and suppressing tumor formation. Therefore, therapeutic strategies aimed at restoring or enhancing HPV16 E2 function may hold promise for the prevention and treatment of HPV-related cancers, including (i) gene-therapy-mediated E2 restoration; (ii) direct delivery of E2 protein; (iii) E2 stabilization through modulation of interacting pathways (e.g., TopBP1, Brd4); and (iv) E2-based therapeutic vaccines. These approaches may exert antitumor effects by repressing E6/E7 oncogenes, regulating the cell cycle, inhibiting cell proliferation, and inducing apoptosis.
papers.abstract_zh: 人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)可引起多种上皮病变,包括宿主细胞甚至宫颈癌的恶性增殖。HPV E2可以在调节病毒基因表达、病毒复制和转录方面发挥重要作用,也可以参与细胞分裂过程中病毒基因组的分离。HPV16 E2蛋白在低分化宫颈病变细胞中高表达,但随着宫颈病变级别的增加而降低或消失。作为DNA复制的起始蛋白和HPV16基因表达的主要转录调节蛋白,E2蛋白可能在病毒生命周期中发挥关键作用。HPV16 E2蛋白作为序列特异性DNA结合蛋白,能够与E6和E7癌基因启动子上的特异性DNA识别序列结合,进而抑制E6和E7癌基因的转录和表达,从而诱导细胞凋亡,抑制肿瘤形成。因此,旨在恢复或增强 HPV16 E2 功能的治疗策略可能有望用于预防和 治疗 HPV 相关癌症,包括(i)基因治疗介导的 E2 恢复;(ii)直接递送E2蛋白;(iii) 通过调节相互作用途径(例如 TopBP1、Brd4)来稳定 E2;(iv) 基于 E2 的治疗剂 疫苗。这些方法可能通过抑制E6/E7癌基因、调节细胞周期、抑制细胞增殖和诱导细胞凋亡来发挥抗肿瘤作用。

papers.title: Beyond analytical proficiency: information continuity gaps in human papillomavirus testing laboratories within China's national external quality assessment network.
papers.abstract: Abstract Objectives External quality assessment (EQA) emphasizes analytical proficiency, but actionable molecular testing also depends on extra-analytical processes that link results to unique patients and subsequent care. We assessed patient de-duplication and downstream-result retrievability in HPV testing laboratories, using EQA performance as an analytical-quality anchor, and explored these capabilities as candidate quality indicators for the total testing process. Methods A voluntary institution-level web survey was embedded in the 2026 National Center for Clinical Laboratories HPV16/18 EQA network and collected 2025 operational data. Survey records were linked to 2025 EQA results. The primary outcome was any laboratory access to downstream cytology, colposcopy, or histopathology information after an HPV-positive result. Associations were examined using prespecified Firth logistic regression, with ordinal and narrower-exposure sensitivity analyses. Results Among 957 unique invitation-frame laboratories, 111 valid responses were obtained; 109 matched the frame (response rate 11 %). Among 89 respondents with 2025 EQA records, 88 (99 %) had fully correct HPV16/18 results. In contrast, 65/111 (59 %) laboratories could retrieve any downstream information, 14/111 (13 %) reported near-complete access, and 41/111 (37 %) could fully de-duplicate repeated tests from the same woman. Clinical service integration was associated with downstream information availability (OR 4.01, 95 % CI 1.71–9.84; p=0.001); the association persisted when exposure was restricted to screening/clinical-reporting functions (OR 3.30, 95 % CI 1.40–8.20; p=0.006). Conclusions High analytical proficiency did not imply closure of the extra-analytical testing loop. Patient identity resolution and downstream-result retrievability merit further standardization and validation as candidate quality indicators for molecular diagnostics and EQA-linked quality improvement.

We assessed patient de-duplication and downstream-result retrievability in HPV testing laboratories, using EQA performance as an analytical-quality anchor, and explored these capabilities as candidate quality indicators for the total testing process. METHODS: A voluntary institution-level web survey was embedded in the 2026 National Center for Clinical Laboratories HPV16/18 EQA network and collected 2025 operational data. Survey records were linked to 2025 EQA results. The primary outcome was any laboratory access to downstream cytology, colposcopy, or histopathology information after an HPV-positive result. Associations were examined using prespecified Firth logistic regression, with ordinal and narrower-exposure sensitivity analyses. RESULTS: Among 957 unique invitation-frame laboratories, 111 valid responses were obtained; 109 matched the frame (response rate 11 %). Among 89 respondents with 2025 EQA records, 88 (99 %) had fully correct HPV16/18 results. In contrast, 65/111 (59 %) laboratories could retrieve any downstream information, 14/111 (13 %) reported near-complete access, and 41/111 (37 %) could fully de-duplicate repeated tests from the same woman. Clinical service integration was associated with downstream information availability (OR 4.01, 95 % CI 1.71-9.84; p=0.001); the association persisted when exposure was restricted to screening/clinical-reporting functions (OR 3.30, 95 % CI 1.40-8.20; p=0.006). CONCLUSIONS: High analytical proficiency did not imply closure of the extra-analytical testing loop. Patient identity resolution and downstream-result retrievability merit further standardization and validation as candidate quality indicators for molecular diagnostics and EQA-linked quality improvement.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on human papillomaviruses (HPV) and evaluates the continuity of information in HPV testing laboratories within China's national external quality assessment (EQA) network. The central question is whether laboratories can effectively link HPV test results to downstream clinical processes such as cytology, colposcopy, or histopathology, and whether these capabilities can serve as quality indicators for the total testing process.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review used a voluntary institution-level web survey embedded in the 2026 National Center for Clinical Laboratories HPV16/18 EQA network. It collected 2025 operational data and linked survey records to EQA results. Associations were analyzed using prespecified Firth logistic regression with ordinal and narrower-exposure sensitivity analyses.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Among 957 unique invitation-frame laboratories, 111 valid responses were obtained, with 109 matching the frame (response rate 11%). The review found that 88% of respondents had fully correct HPV16/18 results. However, only 59% of laboratories could retrieve any downstream information, 13% had near-complete access, and 37% could fully de-duplicate repeated tests from the same woman. Clinical service integration was associated with downstream information availability (OR 4.01, 95% CI 1.71–9.84; p=0.001), and this association remained significant when exposure was restricted to screening/clinical-reporting functions (OR 3.30, 95% CI 1.40–8.20; p=0.006).
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review highlights heterogeneity in the ability of HPV testing laboratories to retrieve downstream clinical information and de-duplicate repeated tests. It notes that only 59% of laboratories could retrieve any downstream information, and 37% could fully de-duplicate repeated tests. These findings suggest unresolved gaps in information continuity and the need for further standardization and validation of these capabilities as quality indicators.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review emphasizes the need for further standardization and validation of patient identity resolution and downstream-result retrievability as candidate quality indicators for molecular diagnostics and EQA-linked quality improvement. It suggests that these processes should be prioritized for research and practice to enhance the overall quality and utility of HPV testing in clinical settings.

analysis.summary_en: This review evaluates the continuity of information in human papillomavirus (HPV) testing laboratories within China's national external quality assessment (EQA) network. It highlights that while analytical proficiency is high, extra-analytical processes such as linking test results to downstream clinical information and de-duplicating repeated tests remain underdeveloped. The study found that only 59% of laboratories could retrieve downstream information, and 37% could fully de-duplicate tests. Clinical service integration was associated with downstream information availability, suggesting the need for further standardization and validation of these processes as quality indicators. The review underscores the importance of improving information continuity to enhance the overall quality and utility of HPV testing in clinical settings.

elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 该综述强调需要进一步标准化和验证患者身份解析和下游结果可检索性,作为分子诊断和 EQA 相关质量改进的候选质量指标。它建议这些过程应优先用于研究和实践,以提高临床环境中 HPV 检测的整体质量和实用性。

papers.title: Neues zu humanen Papillomaviren in der Kopf-Hals-Onkologie – Highlights der ASCO-Jahrestagung 2026 Latest developments in human papillomavirus in head and neck oncology—highlights from the 2026 ASCO Annual Meeting
papers.abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV)-associated oropharyngeal cancer remains one of the most dynamic areas of research in head and neck oncology. While classical de-escalation strategies have been the primary focus of research in recent years, the 2026 American Society of Clinical Oncology (ASCO) Annual Meeting revealed a significant shift toward biologically and immunologically driven treatment approaches. The focus was on new data regarding curative-intent immunotherapy, therapeutic HPV vaccines, innovative biomarkers, and adaptive de-escalation strategies. Of particular note are the results of the randomized phase II KEYCHAIN trial, in which systemic therapy with cisplatin was replaced by immunotherapy as part of the primary treatment for advanced p16-positive head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC). This study provided the first positive evidence in favor of a PD‐1 inhibitor with regard to the primary endpoint of progression-free survival, while also demonstrating lower toxicity. This contrasted with the negative results of the HN.9 study, in which primary radioimmunotherapy failed to meet the primary endpoint of event-free survival. Furthermore, promising data on Immunoscore-based risk models and therapeutic vaccination strategies were presented.

papers.title: Genome-wide association study of human papillomavirus infection and persistence in women living with HIV in Rwanda.
papers.abstract: Abstract Background We conducted an explorative genome-wide association study (GWAS) in East Africa to identify host genetic variants associated with the acquisition and persistence of human papillomavirus (HPV) infection. Methods We genotyped 385 Rwandan women living with HIV and selected host biomarker assay signals from genital swab samples using qPCR. We compared women who cleared HPV over a two-year interval (operationally defined as persistent infection), with those who did not. Exploratory gene-based aggregation analyses of rare and low-frequency variants represented on the genotyping array were also performed. Results In the primary cluster-stratified Cochran–Mantel–Haenszel analysis, rs13158830 within PPARGC1B exceeded the conventional genome-wide significance threshold for persistent HPV infection. The nearby MIR378A gene-expression assay signal was higher in HPV-positive women but did not distinguish clearance from persistence. Conclusions We identified an exploratory host genetic association with persistent HPV infection and several additional candidate loci. The lead rs13158830 signal remained evident in Fisher exact testing and PC-adjusted Firth regression, but the small number of carriers produced substantial uncertainty. These findings require replication in independent cohorts. Clinical trial registration Not applicable.

papers.title: Population-Level Shifts in Cervical Cancer Stage Distribution in the United States Following Human Papillomavirus (HPV) Vaccine Implementation.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To assess whether human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine introduction is associated with shifts in stage at cervical cancer diagnosis and to examine whether sociodemographic disparities and evolving imaging practices have influenced these observed trends. METHODS: We analyzed 103,831 cervical cancer cases diagnosed between January 2004 and December 2022 from the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) database. Stage at diagnosis was classified as non-distant or distant disease and compared across sociodemographic subgroups, including age group at diagnosis (<40 vs. ≥40 years), race/ethnicity, income, and urban-rural status. Temporal trends in distant-stage disease were evaluated using a linear probability model including year of diagnosis, age group, and an age group-by-year interaction term. RESULTS: Across the entire cohort (N = 103,831), 14,622 patients (14.1%) presented with distant-stage disease. Among patients <40 years, distant disease increased from 5.6% in 2004 to 9.2% in 2022, corresponding to an annual increase of 0.18 percentage points per year (95% CI 0.12-0.23, p < 0.001). Among patients ≥40 years, distant disease increased from 12.6% in 2004 to 20.4% in 2022, corresponding to an annual increase of 0.39 percentage points per year (95% CI 0.34-0.44, p < 0.001). The annual increase was 0.21 percentage points greater among patients ≥40 years (95% CI 0.14-0.29, interaction p < 0.001). CONCLUSION: Over the past two decades, distant-stage cervical cancer increased in the United States, with a significantly steeper increase among women ≥40 years than among women <40 years. The comparatively smaller increase among younger women is consistent with a possible contribution of HPV vaccination at the population level; however, individual vaccination status was unavailable, and a causal relationship cannot be established. Persistent racial, socioeconomic, and geographic disparities in distant-stage presentation emphasize the ongoing need for equitable access to vaccination and screening.

papers.title: Baseline HPV16 status and genotype multiplicity independently predict subsequent high-grade cervical lesions in HR-HPV-positive women referred for colposcopy with negative or low-grade cytology: A prospective cohort study.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the prospective risk of high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion or worse (HSIL+) in high-risk HPV (HR-HPV)positive women, assessing the independent and interactive effects of baseline HPV16-status, genotype multiplicity, and follow-up HPV persistence. METHODS: A prospective cohort of 2562 HR-HPV-positive women referred for colposcopy were categorized into four groups: single non-HPV16, single HPV16, HPV16 plus other HR types, or multiple non-HPV16. HSIL+ risk was analysed using Cox-proportional-hazards-regression, restricted mean survival time (RMST) at 36months, and Fine-Gray competing-risk models. Multivariable logistic regression evaluated concurrent HSIL+ risk associated with follow-up HPV persistence. RESULTS: Overall, 691 women (27.0%) developed HSIL+. Infection with HPV16 plus other HR types carried the highest risk (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR]2.10, 95%CI: 1.69-2.62) and shorter median HSIL+-free survival than single non-HPV16 infection (24 vs. 54months), corresponding to 5.1 fewer HSIL+-free-months at 36months (p<0.001). Baseline HPV16 positivity and genotype multiplicity exerted independent, additive effects without multiplicative interaction (adjusted p=0.600). Incorporating multiplicity improved model discrimination beyond entry cytology and HPV16 status (concordance index 0.612 vs. Results remained robust in competing-risk analyses (subdistribution HR2.03, 95%CI: 1.64-2.52) and after excluding early-treated women (aHR2.00, 95%CI: 1.52-2.62). Follow-up viral persistence strongly correlated with concurrent HSIL+ (aHR5.71-8.59, p<0.001), reflecting a cross-sectional risk correlation complementary to baseline prognostication. CONCLUSIONS: Baseline HPV16 positivity and genotype multiplicity are independent, additive risk factors for HSIL+, with HPV16 plus other HR types marking the highest-risk subgroup. Genotype multiplicity provides distinct clinical predictive value alongside HPV16 status, while follow-up HPV persistence offers complementary, non-redundant information for concurrent risk evaluation in risk-based management strategies.

papers.title: HPV Infection in Sub-Saharan Africa: Circulating Genotypes, Vaccination Strategies (Single-Dose Versus Two-Dose), and Implications of HIV Co-Infection
papers.abstract: Cervical cancer is a major cause of morbidity and mortality among women in sub-Saharan Africa, where vaccination coverage remains below the World Health Or-ganization target of 90% of girls fully vaccinated by 15 years of age. This narrative review synthesizes evidence on HPV genotype distribution, single-dose versus two-dose vac-cination, and the implications of HIV co-infection. Although HPV16 and HPV18 remain the predominant oncogenic types, HPV35, HPV52, HPV45, HPV33, and HPV58 are re-ported frequently in sub-Saharan African populations. Consequently, some high-risk infections fall outside bivalent and quadrivalent vaccine coverage, and some detected types remain outside nonavalent vaccine coverage. Randomized trials in Tanzania and Kenya demonstrate durable single-dose immunogenicity through 60 months and vac-cine efficacy above 98% against persistent vaccine-type infection through 54 months, respectively. The ESCUDDO trial in Costa Rica provides a direct five-year randomized comparison showing noninferiority of one dose to two doses. Equivalent single-dose efficacy and durability evidence for people living with HIV remains unavailable. These findings support expanded single-dose vaccination in immunocompetent populations alongside multidose pathways for people living with HIV, genotype-specific surveil-lance, and continued cervical screening.

analysis.summary_en: This review focuses on human papillomaviruses (HPV) in sub-Saharan Africa, emphasizing their role in cervical cancer and the impact of HIV co-infection. It highlights the predominant oncogenic types, such as HPV16 and HPV18, and the frequent detection of other high-risk types like HPV35, HPV52, HPV45, HPV33, and HPV58. Evidence from randomized trials in Tanzania, Kenya, and Costa Rica supports the noninferiority of single-dose vaccination compared to two-dose regimens in immunocompetent populations. However, equivalent efficacy and durability data for people living with HIV are lacking. The review underscores the need for genotype-specific surveillance, continued cervical screening, and tailored vaccination strategies for immunocompromised individuals.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 宫颈癌 是撒哈拉以南非洲地区妇女发病和 死亡率 的主要原因,该地区的 疫苗接种 覆盖率仍低于世界卫生组织设定的 90% 女孩在 15 岁之前完全接种疫苗的目标。这篇叙述性综述综合了 HPV 基因型分布、单剂量与两剂量 疫苗接种 以及 HIV 合并感染的影响的证据。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 坦桑尼亚和肯尼亚的随机试验分别证明了 60 个月内的持久单剂量免疫原性,以及 54 个月内 疫苗 对持续 疫苗 型感染的功效分别高于 98%。哥斯达黎加的 ESCUDDO 试验提供了直接的五年随机比较,显示一剂与两剂的非劣效性。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 尽管 HPV16 和 HPV18 仍然是主要的致癌类型,但 HPV35、HPV52、HPV45、HPV33 和 HPV58 在撒哈拉以南非洲人群中也经常报告。对于艾滋病毒感染者来说,尚无等效的单剂量疗效和持久性证据。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 因此,一些高风险感染不在二价和四价 疫苗 覆盖范围内,而一些检测到的类型仍然在非无价 疫苗 覆盖范围之外。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 这些发现支持在免疫功能正常人群中扩大单剂量 疫苗接种,以及针对 HIV 感染者的多剂量途径、基因型特异性 监测 以及持续的宫颈筛查。

papers.title: Integrated Genomic and Immune Profiling Reveals PIK3CA-Mutant HPV16-Positive Cervical Cancer as a Clinically Aggressive and Immunologically Distinct Subtype in Patients from Eastern India
papers.abstract: Background: HPV16-driven cervical cancer (CaCx) is a leading cause of cancer-related mortality among Indian women. Identifying population-specific genomic and immune determinants may improve therapeutic strategies. Methods: We performed whole-exome sequencing on 49 HPV16-positive cervical tumors and matched blood samples. Available RNA-seq data from 29 out of 49 tumors were integrated, to identify recurrent mutations, altered pathways, and immune microenvironment features. Results: We identified 6,462 somatic mutations enriched in cancer-related pathways, particularly PI3K-Akt signaling. PIK3CA was the most recurrently mutated gene (42%), significantly higher frequency (p < 0.04) than in HPV16-positive TCGA-CESC tumors (26.21%). Unlike TCGA-CESC, where PIK3CA mutations were associated with early-stage disease, Indian PIK3CA-mutant tumors were enriched in advanced-stage disease. These tumors exhibited lower viral loads, higher tumor mutation burden, and more aggressive molecular phenotypes than PIK3CA-wild tumors. CIBERSORT-based immune profiling showed comparable immune-cell infiltration, including CD8+ T cells, between PIK3CA-mutant tumors and normal tissues, whereas PIK3CA-wild tumors showed significantly enhanced infiltration, compared to normal tissues. Both tumor subtypes portrayed mature tertiary lymphoid structures at higher levels than normal tissues. Compared to normal tissues, CD274 (PD-L1) expression was elevated significantly in both subtypes, while PDCD1 (PD-1) upregulation and PD-1/PD-L1 transcriptional coupling at significant levels, occurred exclusively in PIK3CA-mutant tumors. The CCL3-CCR1 axis was selectively activated in PIK3CA-mutant tumors and correlated with cytotoxic, interferon-response, myeloid, and immune checkpoint markers, indicating an immunosuppressive microenvironment. Conclusion: PIK3CA mutations define a molecularly aggressive, immunologically distinct subtype of HPV16-positive CaCx in Indian patients, underscoring their potential for targeted therapeutic interventions.

CIBERSORT-based immune profiling showed comparable immune-cell infiltration, including CD8+ T cells, between PIK3CA-mutant tumors and normal tissues, whereas PIK3CA-wild tumors showed significantly enhanced infiltration, compared to normal tissues. Compared to normal tissues, CD274 (PD-L1) expression was elevated significantly in both subtypes, while PDCD1 (PD-1) upregulation and PD-1/PD-L1 transcriptional coupling at significant levels, occurred exclusively in PIK3CA-mutant tumors. papers.title: First-void urine testing for high-risk human papillomavirus: A within-cohort comparison of three preanalytical approaches.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To compare three preanalytical approaches for first-void urine (FVU)-based high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) DNA detection against paired cervical swab (CS) specimens. METHODS: This cross-sectional observational study included 69 participants with a previous positive hrHPV screening result and paired CS and FVU specimens. From each FVU specimen, three urine preparations were generated: unpreserved urine, EDTA-treated urine for DNA stabilization, urine buffered with urine conservation medium (UCM; Novosanis, Wijnegem, Belgium). All specimens were analyzed using the QIAscreen HPV PCR Test (Qiagen, Hilden, Germany). Agreement with paired CS specimens, genotype-specific agreement, paired CS cycle threshold (Ct) values, and participant-reported perceptions of urine sampling were assessed. RESULTS: Overall agreement between urine and CS specimens was moderate across all three approaches, with Cohen's κ values of 0.566 for unpreserved urine, 0.538 for EDTA-treated urine, and 0.581 for UCM-buffered urine. Paired CS Ct values were lower in participants with hrHPV DNA-positive urine specimens than in those with hrHPV DNA-negative urine specimens, consistent with greater urinary detectability at higher cervical hrHPV DNA levels. Genotype-specific agreement was stronger for HPV16 and HPV18 than for pooled non-16/18 hrHPV. Participant-reported data suggested good acceptability of urine sampling. CONCLUSIONS: The three approaches showed broadly similar results to one another, while agreement with paired CS specimens was moderate across all approaches. These findings support further evaluation of urine-based hrHPV testing as a non-invasive sampling option that could help expand access to testing, particularly in low-income and other resource-limited settings.

source_records.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To compare three preanalytical approaches for first-void urine (FVU)-based high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) DNA detection against paired cervical swab (CS) specimens. METHODS: This cross-sectional observational study included 69 participants with a previous positive hrHPV screening result and paired CS and FVU specimens. From each FVU specimen, three urine preparations were generated: unpreserved urine, EDTA-treated urine for DNA stabilization, urine buffered with urine conservation medium (UCM; Novosanis, Wijnegem, Belgium). All specimens were analyzed using the QIAscreen HPV PCR Test (Qiagen, Hilden, Germany). Agreement with paired CS specimens, genotype-specific agreement, paired CS cycle threshold (Ct) values, and participant-reported perceptions of urine sampling were assessed. RESULTS: Overall agreement between urine and CS specimens was moderate across all three approaches, with Cohen's κ values of 0.566 for unpreserved urine, 0.538 for EDTA-treated urine, and 0.581 for UCM-buffered urine. Paired CS Ct values were lower in participants with hrHPV DNA-positive urine specimens than in those with hrHPV DNA-negative urine specimens, consistent with greater urinary detectability at higher cervical hrHPV DNA levels. Genotype-specific agreement was stronger for HPV16 and HPV18 than for pooled non-16/18 hrHPV. Participant-reported data suggested good acceptability of urine sampling. CONCLUSIONS: The three approaches showed broadly similar results to one another, while agreement with paired CS specimens was moderate across all approaches. These findings support further evaluation of urine-based hrHPV testing as a non-invasive sampling option that could help expand access to testing, particularly in low-income and other resource-limited settings.

papers.abstract_zh: 目的:比较基于首次排尿 (FVU) 的高危 人乳头瘤病毒 (hrHPV) DNA 检测与配对宫颈拭子 (CS) 样本的三种分析前方法。方法:这项横断面观察性研究包括 69 名先前 hrHPV 筛查结果呈阳性的参与者以及配对的 CS 和 FVU 样本。从每个 FVU 样本中,生成三种尿液制剂:未保存的尿液、用于 DNA 稳定的 EDTA 处理尿液、用尿液保存介质缓冲的尿液(UCM;Novosanis,Wijnegem,比利时)。所有样本均使用 QIAscreen HPV PCR 检测(Qiagen,希尔登,德国)进行分析。评估了配对 CS 样本的一致性、基因型特异性一致性、配对 CS 周期阈值 (Ct) 值以及参与者报告的尿液采样感知。结果:在所有三种方法中,尿液和 CS 样本之间的总体一致性中等,未保存尿液的 Cohen κ 值为 0.566,EDTA 处理尿液为 0.538,UCM 缓冲尿液为 0.581。hrHPV DNA 阳性尿液样本的配对 CS Ct 值低于 hrHPV DNA 阴性尿液样本的参与者,这与宫颈 hrHPV DNA 水平较高时尿液可检出率较高一致。HPV16 和 HPV18 的基因型特异性一致性比合并的非 16/18 hrHPV 更强。参与者报告的数据表明尿液采样的可接受性良好。结论:这三种方法显示出彼此大致相似的结果,而所有方法与配对 CS 样本的一致性中等。这些发现支持进一步评估基于尿液的 hrHPV 检测作为一种非侵入性采样选择,有助于扩大检测范围,特别是在低收入和其他资源有限的环境中。

papers.title: Urine and menstrual blood as noninvasive alternatives for human papillomavirus detection: a literature review
papers.abstract: At present, middle-and low-income countries including Mexico, are still using cervical smear or Pap as the first screening test for early cervical cancer and its precursor lesions detection.In addition, there are primary prevention programs that include vaccination against human papillomavirus (HPV), targeting girls and boys, as well as certain vulnerable groups.As part of the efforts to address and eliminate this health problem, research networks in various developed countries are focusing on new procedures that can help resolve this issue, and, in addition to the Pap test, they are already routinely performing molecular HPV testing.However, the availability of supplies and trained personnel for molecular or biochemical tests, as well as the psychosocial obstacles could be some challenges.Therefore, it is essential to implement novel methods for the collection of human fluids sample and for conducting molecular HPV tests in low-income countries with diverse cultural contexts.In this context, non-invasive self-collection of the sample could be a viable, affordable, and accurate solution for detecting the primary etiological factor of cervical lesions; thus, the early detection of those pathologies would potentially have a global impact.This review presents data supporting and justifying the present alternatives; it is not a fashion; it is a necessity.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on human papillomaviruses (HPV) and their association with cervical cancer and related diseases. The central question is whether urine and menstrual blood can serve as non-invasive alternatives for HPV detection, particularly in low- and middle-income countries where traditional methods like Pap tests are still widely used. The topic boundary is restricted to HPV types and explicitly HPV-associated diseases, excluding generic cancers unless they are specifically linked to HPV.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a literature review that presents data supporting the use of non-invasive sample collection methods for HPV detection. It does not explicitly report on the databases used, search dates, or eligibility criteria for included studies. The review method is narrative, with no mention of meta-analysis or systematic review techniques.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that non-invasive self-collection methods, such as urine and menstrual blood, could be a viable, affordable, and accurate solution for detecting HPV in low-income countries. It emphasizes the importance of these methods in improving early detection of cervical lesions and reducing the barriers associated with traditional Pap tests.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review acknowledges that the availability of supplies and trained personnel for molecular HPV testing remains a challenge in low-income countries. Additionally, it notes that psychosocial obstacles may hinder the adoption of these new methods. There is no explicit mention of conflicting findings or unresolved mechanisms, but the review highlights the need for further research to address these limitations.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review suggests that implementing novel methods for sample collection and molecular HPV testing in low-income countries could have a significant global impact. It implies the need for research and development to improve accessibility and affordability of these tests, as well as to address psychosocial barriers to their adoption.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the potential of urine and menstrual blood as non-invasive alternatives for detecting human papillomavirus (HPV), particularly in low- and middle-income countries where traditional Pap tests are still prevalent. It highlights the importance of these methods in early detection of cervical lesions and the challenges associated with their implementation, such as limited supplies and trained personnel. The review underscores the necessity of adopting these alternatives to improve HPV screening and prevention efforts, especially in diverse cultural contexts. It calls for further research to address the logistical and psychosocial barriers to their widespread use.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述重点关注 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 及其与 宫颈癌 及相关疾病的关联。核心问题是尿液和经血是否可以作为 HPV 检测的非侵入性替代方案,特别是在仍广泛使用巴氏试验等传统方法的低收入​​和中等收入国家。主题范围仅限于 HPV 类型和明确与 HPV 相关的疾病,不包括一般癌症,除非它们与 HPV 特别相关。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述是一篇文献综述,提供了支持使用非侵入性样本采集方法进行 HPV 检测的数据。它没有明确报告所使用的数据库、检索日期或纳入研究的资格标准。审查方法是叙述性的,没有提及荟萃分析或系统审查技术。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 审查得出的结论是,尿液和经血等非侵入性自我采集方法可能是低收入国家检测 HPV 的可行、负担得起且准确的解决方案。它强调了这些方法在改善宫颈病变的早期检测和减少与传统巴氏试验相关的障碍方面的重要性。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该审查承认,分子 HPV 检测的用品和训练有素的人员的可用性仍然是低收入国家的一个挑战。此外,它指出社会心理障碍可能会阻碍这些新方法的采用。没有明确提及相互矛盾的发现或未解决的机制,但该评论强调需要进一步研究来解决这些局限性。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 审查表明,在低收入国家实施样本采集和分子 HPV 检测的新方法可能会对全球产生重大影响。这意味着需要进行研究和开发,以提高这些测试的可及性和可负担性,并解决采用这些测试的社会心理障碍。

papers.title: Multilevel factors associated with human papillomavirus vaccination coverage in Iowa youth: Evidence from a statewide immunization registry.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination at the earliest opportunity is critical for preventing cervical, vulvar, vaginal, anal, rectal, and oropharyngeal cancers. This study examined individual-level and area-level factors associated with HPV vaccination among Iowa youth. METHODS: We analyzed Iowa Immunization Registry Information System data for youth aged 9-17 years, linked to ZIP Code Tabulation Area socioeconomic and demographic measures. Hierarchical Bayesian spatial models estimated HPV vaccination initiation, completion at any age, and on-time completion. RESULTS: Receipt of school-required and other routinely recommended vaccines was strongly associated with HPV vaccination. Compared with youth who received both vaccine types, those who received only school-required vaccines or only other routinely recommended vaccines had lower HPV vaccination odds (ORs = 0.01-0.42, 95% CrIs = [0.01, 0.43]). Female youth, insured youth, and those of Hispanic or Latino ethnicity had higher vaccination odds. Youth in rural, small town, and micropolitan areas had lower odds than those in metropolitan areas (ORs = 0.89-0.93, 95% CrIs = [0.85, 0.97]). Area-level education, housing, and local HPV vaccination rates were associated with vaccination. CONCLUSIONS: Individual-level and area-level characteristics were associated with HPV vaccination. Interventions promoting preventive care and routine youth vaccination while addressing geographic disparities may improve vaccine coverage and reduce HPV-related cancer risk.

papers.title: Factors associated with oral HPV infection and clearance in people living with HIV and populations at increased risk of HIV acquisition: a systematic review and meta-analysis
papers.abstract: Background Oral human papillomavirus (HPV) infection precedes most HPV-related oropharyngeal cancers, but determinants of oral HPV prevalence and incidence in people living with HIV (PLWH) and populations at increased risk of HIV acquisition remain unclear. Methods PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched through July 10, 2026, for observational studies of laboratory-confirmed oral HPV prevalence, incidence, or clearance in adults with or at risk for HIV. Adjusted estimates were pooled by random-effects meta-analysis and assessed with GRADE. Results Twenty-seven studies with a cumulative reported sample size of 13,625 participants were included, of which 25 contributed to the meta-analysis. For oral HPV prevalence, smoking (n = 8; OR, 2.11; 95% CI, 1.58–2.83), HIV infection (n = 6; OR, 2.44; 95% CI, 1.69–3.52), and lower CD4 count (n = 8; OR, 3.02; 95% CI, 2.10–4.35) were significantly associated with higher odds, whereas alcohol, recent oral-sex partners, and HIV viral load were not. For oral HPV incidence, more recent oral-sex partners (n = 3; HR, 1.88; 95% CI, 1.41–2.49), more lifetime oral-sex partners (n = 3; HR, 2.19; 95% CI, 1.03–4.68), HIV infection (n = 2; HR, 1.90; 95% CI, 1.20–3.02), lower CD4 count (n = 4; HR, 1.85; 95% CI, 1.43–2.40), and higher HIV viral load (n = 2; HR, 2.51; 95% CI, 1.28–4.93) were significantly associated with increased incidence, whereas smoking and alcohol were not. HIV infection showed a borderline association with reduced clearance (n = 3; HR, 0.43; 95% CI, 0.19–1.00). Certainty of evidence ranged from low to very low. Conclusions Smoking was associated with oral HPV prevalence, whereas greater oral-sex exposure and higher HIV viral load were more clearly associated with incidence. HIV infection and lower CD4 counts were associated with both outcomes, while evidence for clearance remained inconclusive. Further prospective studies are needed.

papers.title: Persistent HPV16 E7 Expression Establishes a Preconditioned Epithelial State and Reveals Amplified Transcriptional Responses in Females During Oral Carcinogenesis
papers.abstract: Abstract Human papillomavirus (HPV)-associated and carcinogen-driven head and neck squamous cell carcinomas (HNSCC) arise through distinct biological routes, yet how each aetiology shapes the tissue state in which carcinogenesis begins remains unclear. We investigated how HPV16 E7 oncoprotein expression and biological sex influence the oral epithelial response before and during carcinogen exposure. Oral epithelium from male and female wild-type (WT) and HPV16 E7-expressing transgenic (K14E7) mice was analysed before and following 4-nitroquinoline-1-oxide (4NQO) induced oral carcinogenesis using flow cytometry, histopathology, immunohistochemistry, and RNA sequencing, with transcriptional programmes compared with human HPV + and HPV − HNSCC. Persistent HPV16 E7 expression established epithelial hyperplasia and a baseline transcriptional state enriched for cell-cycle, MYC, interferon response and inflammatory programmes, accompanied by selective remodelling of T cell and myeloid cells. HPV16 E7-driven transcriptional remodelling was more pronounced in females, although pathway enrichment was conserved between sexes. Following 4NQO exposure, WT epithelium underwent transcriptional remodelling that recapitulated programmes already active in untreated K14E7 epithelium, whereas K14E7 epithelium showed limited additional transcriptional change despite similar pathological endpoints. Cross-species analyses showed concordance between the murine WT and K14E7 4NQO model and human HPV − and HPV + HNSCC, with sex-associated pathways demonstrating significant, albeit more modest, cross-species concordance. Together, these findings indicate that HPV16 E7 establishes a preconditioned proliferative and inflammatory epithelial state with early immune remodelling that alters responses to carcinogenic injury. HPV16 E7 may redirect rather than accelerate epithelial remodelling during carcinogenesis, with female transcriptional responsiveness to both oncogene expression and carcinogen exposure emerging as a feature of epithelial adaptation.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to understand how HPV16 E7 oncoprotein expression and biological sex influence the oral epithelial response before and during carcinogen exposure. The background highlights that HPV-associated and carcinogen-driven head and neck squamous cell carcinomas (HNSCC) arise through distinct biological routes, yet the tissue state shaped by each aetiology remains unclear.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study used oral epithelium from male and female wild-type (WT) and HPV16 E7-expressing transgenic (K14E7) mice, analysing them before and following 4-nitroquinoline-1-oxide (4NQO) induced oral carcinogenesis. The population included both sexes and two genetic models, with comparisons made to human HPV + and HPV − HNSCC.
analysis.methods: The methods involved flow cytometry, histopathology, immunohistochemistry, and RNA sequencing to analyse oral epithelium from mice. Transcriptional programmes were compared with human HPV + and HPV − HNSCC to assess differences in biological responses.
analysis.main_results: Persistent HPV16 E7 expression established epithelial hyperplasia and a baseline transcriptional state enriched for cell-cycle, MYC, interferon response and inflammatory programmes. These changes were accompanied by selective remodelling of T cell and myeloid cells.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that HPV16 E7 establishes a preconditioned proliferative and inflammatory epithelial state with early immune remodelling, altering responses to carcinogenic injury. This indicates that HPV16 E7 may redirect rather than accelerate epithelial remodelling during carcinogenesis.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results provide insights into the molecular mechanisms by which HPV16 E7 influences the progression of oral carcinogenesis, which could inform future research on HPV-associated cancers and the development of targeted therapies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to mouse models and does not directly translate to human outcomes. However, cross-species analyses showed concordance between the murine model and human HPV − and HPV + HNSCC, supporting a moderate confidence in the findings.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates how HPV16 E7 oncoprotein expression and biological sex influence the oral epithelial response before and during carcinogen exposure. Using mouse models, the research reveals that persistent HPV16 E7 expression establishes a preconditioned proliferative and inflammatory state, with more pronounced transcriptional remodelling in females. The findings suggest that HPV16 E7 may redirect rather than accelerate epithelial remodelling during carcinogenesis, highlighting sex-associated differences in immune and transcriptional responses. While the study is based on animal models, cross-species analyses showed concordance with human HPV-associated head and neck squamous cell carcinomas (HNSCC), indicating potential implications for understanding HPV-driven cancer progression. The study's results are supported by RNA sequencing and comparative analyses, though limitations include the reliance on mouse models and the absence of direct human clinical data.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在了解 HPV16 E7 癌蛋白表达和生物性别如何影响致癌物暴露之前和期间的口腔上皮反应。背景强调,HPV 相关且致癌物驱动的头颈鳞状细胞癌 (HNSCC) 通过不同的生物学途径产生,但每种病因形成的组织状态仍不清楚。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究使用雄性和雌性野生型 (WT) 和表达 HPV16 E7 的转基因 (K14E7) 小鼠的口腔上皮,对 4-硝基喹啉-1-氧化物 (4NQO) 诱导口腔癌发生前后的口腔上皮进行分析。该人群包括两种性别和两种遗传模型,并与人类 HPV + 和 HPV - HNSCC 进行比较。
elements_zh.methods: 这些方法涉及流式细胞术、组织病理学、免疫组织化学和 RNA 测序来分析小鼠的口腔上皮。将转录程序与人类 HPV + 和 HPV - HNSCC 进行比较,以评估生物反应的差异。
elements_zh.main_results: 持续的 HPV16 E7 表达建立了上皮增生和丰富细胞周期、MYC、干扰素反应和炎症程序的基线转录状态。这些变化伴随着 T 细胞和骨髓细胞的选择性重塑。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,HPV16 E7 通过早期免疫重塑建立了一种预处理的增殖和炎症上皮状态,改变了对致癌损伤的反应。这表明HPV16 E7可能在癌变过程中重定向而不是加速上皮重塑。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果提供了有关 HPV16 E7 影响口腔癌发生进展的分子机制的见解,这可以为未来有关 HPV 相关癌症的研究和靶向治疗的开发提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于小鼠模型,并不能直接转化为人类结果。然而,跨物种分析显示小鼠模型与人类 HPV - 和 HPV + HNSCC 之间的一致性,支持对研究结果的中等可信度。

HPV16 E7 may redirect rather than accelerate epithelial remodelling during carcinogenesis, with female transcriptional responsiveness to both oncogene expression and carcinogen exposure emerging as a feature of epithelial adaptation.

papers.title: The assembly pathway for human papillomavirus L1 capsid protein is encoded in electrostatic interactions.
papers.abstract: Human papillomavirus L1 protein spontaneously folds and assembles into 60 nm virus-like particles (VLP), with T = 7d icosahedral symmetry at high salt concentrations but not in low salt. Rapid increase from low to high salt during the assembly process gives poor-quality VLPs, while slowly increasing salt, over as many as 48 h, gives rise to high-quality VLPs. Insight into this behavior is drawn from a computational model based on the cryogenic electron microscopy (cryo-EM) structure of the human papillomavirus Type 16 VLP. Electrostatic potential energy barriers were calculated using the linearized Poisson-Boltzmann equation. After initial, rapid oligomerization of monomers into symmetrical pentamers (capsomeres), these units form pairwise interactions in energetic order, lowest barrier first. But at high salt concentrations, the energetic barriers are more or less equal and irregular particles form, both in simulation and in experiments. The interaction interfaces were modified by mutation to favor the smaller, 30 nm T = 1 icosahedral symmetry and disfavor T = 7d symmetry. The results were smaller particles. By carefully controlling ionic strength, and/or by mutating interface residues by design, it is possible to make high quality, highly immunogenic VLPs directly from unpurified bacterial lysate, without requiring the use of a disassembly/reassembly step.
papers.journal: Protein science : a publication of the Protein Society

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to understand the assembly pathway of human papillomavirus L1 capsid protein and how salt concentration affects the formation of virus-like particles (VLPs). The research was motivated by the need to improve the quality of VLPs for vaccine development.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study used a computational model based on the cryogenic electron microscopy (cryo-EM) structure of the human papillomavirus Type 16 VLP to investigate the assembly pathway. The model simulated the effects of varying salt concentrations on the formation of VLPs.
analysis.methods: The assembly process was modeled using computational methods, and electrostatic potential energy barriers were calculated using the linearized Poisson-Boltzmann equation. Mutations were introduced to modify interaction interfaces and test their impact on VLP symmetry.
analysis.main_results: The results showed that rapid increases in salt concentration led to poor-quality VLPs, while slow increases over 48 hours produced high-quality VLPs. Mutations were found to favor the smaller, 30 nm T = 1 icosahedral symmetry and disfavor T = 7d symmetry.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that the assembly pathway is governed by electrostatic interactions and that controlling ionic strength or mutating specific residues can lead to the formation of high-quality, immunogenic VLPs directly from bacterial lysate.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings have implications for the production of VLPs for HPV vaccines, as they suggest that careful control of salt concentration and targeted mutations can improve the quality of VLPs without the need for disassembly and reassembly steps.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on computational modeling and experimental validation, which may have limitations in fully capturing the complexity of in vivo assembly processes. The evidence is moderate due to the reliance on simulations and the absence of direct clinical outcomes.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the assembly pathway of human papillomavirus (HPV) L1 capsid protein, focusing on how salt concentration influences the formation of virus-like particles (VLPs). The research highlights that rapid salt increases lead to poor-quality VLPs, while slow increases over 48 hours produce high-quality ones. Computational modeling based on cryo-EM data of HPV16 VLPs was used to analyze electrostatic interactions. Mutations were introduced to modify interaction interfaces, favoring T = 1 symmetry and disfavoring T = 7d. The findings suggest that controlling ionic strength and mutating specific residues can enhance VLP quality for vaccine development. The study's evidence is moderate due to its reliance on simulations and the absence of direct clinical outcomes.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究使用基于 人乳头瘤病毒 16 型 VLP 低温电子显微镜 (cryo-EM) 结构的计算模型来研究组装途径。该模型模拟了不同盐浓度对 VLP 形成的影响。
elements_zh.methods: 使用计算方法对组装过程进行建模,并使用线性化泊松-玻尔兹曼方程计算静电势能垒。引入 突变 来修改交互界面并测试其对 VLP 对称性的影响。
elements_zh.main_results: 结果表明,盐浓度的快速增加会导致VLP质量较差,而在48小时内缓慢增加盐浓度会产生高质量的VLP。发现 突变 有利于较小的 30 nm T = 1 二十面体对称性,而不利于 T = 7d 对称性。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,组装途径受静电相互作用控制,控制离子强度或突变特定残基可以导致直接从细菌裂解物中形成高质量、免疫原性的 VLP。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现对 HPV 疫苗 的 VLP 生产具有影响,因为它们表明,仔细控制盐浓度和靶向 突变 可以提高 VLP 的质量,而无需拆卸和重新组装步骤。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究基于计算模型和实验验证,在充分捕捉体内组装过程的复杂性方面可能存在局限性。由于依赖模拟且缺乏直接的临床结果,证据是中等的。

papers.abstract_zh: 人乳头瘤病毒 L1 蛋白自发折叠并组装成 60 nm 病毒样颗粒 (VLP),在高盐浓度下具有 T = 7d 二十面体对称性,但在低盐浓度下则不然。在组装过程中从低盐到高盐的快速增加会产生质量较差的 VLP,而在长达 48 小时内缓慢增加盐会产生高质量的 VLP。对这种行为的深入了解是通过基于 人乳头瘤病毒 16 型 VLP 低温电子显微镜 (cryo-EM) 结构的计算模型得出的。使用线性化泊松-玻尔兹曼方程计算静电势能垒。在单体最初快速寡聚成对称五聚体(壳粒)后,这些单元以能量顺序形成成对相互作用,最低势垒首先。但在高盐浓度下,无论是在模拟还是在实验中,能量势垒或多或少都是相等的,并且粒子形式不规则。相互作用界面由 突变 修改,以支持更小的 30 nm T = 1 二十面体对称性,而不支持 T = 7d 对称性。结果是更小的颗粒。通过仔细控制离子强度和/或通过设计突变界面残基,可以直接从未纯化的细菌裂解物中制备高质量、高免疫原性的VLP,而不需要使用拆卸/重新组装步骤。
papers.summary_zh: 人乳头瘤病毒 L1 蛋白自发折叠并组装成 60 nm 病毒样颗粒 (VLP),在高盐浓度下具有 T = 7d 二十面体对称性,但在低盐浓度下则不然。在组装过程中从低盐到高盐的快速增加会产生质量较差的 VLP,而在长达 48 小时内缓慢增加盐会产生高质量的 VLP。对这种行为的深入了解是通过基于 人乳头瘤病毒 16 型 VLP 低温电子显微镜 (cryo-EM) 结构的计算模型得出的。使用线性化泊松-玻尔兹曼方程计算静电势能垒。在单体最初快速寡聚成对称五聚体(壳粒)后,这些单元以能量顺序形成成对相互作用,最低势垒首先。但在高盐浓度下,无论是在模拟还是在实验中,能量势垒或多或少都是相等的,并且粒子形式不规则。相互作用界面由 突变 修改,以支持更小的 30 nm T = 1 二十面体对称性,而不支持 T = 7d 对称性。结果是更小的颗粒。通过仔细控制离子强度和/或通过设计突变界面残基,可以直接从未纯化的细菌裂解物中制备高质量、高免疫原性的VLP,而不需要使用拆卸/重新组装步骤。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在了解 人乳头瘤病毒 L1 衣壳蛋白的组装途径以及盐浓度如何影响病毒样颗粒 (VLP) 的形成。这项研究的动机是需要提高 疫苗 开发的 VLP 质量。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究使用基于 人乳头瘤病毒 16 型 VLP 低温电子显微镜 (cryo-EM) 结构的计算模型来研究组装途径。该模型模拟了不同盐浓度对 VLP 形成的影响。
analysis_zh.methods: 使用计算方法对组装过程进行建模,并使用线性化泊松-玻尔兹曼方程计算静电势能垒。引入 突变 来修改交互界面并测试其对 VLP 对称性的影响。
analysis_zh.main_results: 结果表明,盐浓度的快速增加会导致VLP质量较差,而在48小时内缓慢增加盐浓度会产生高质量的VLP。发现 突变 有利于较小的 30 nm T = 1 二十面体对称性,而不利于 T = 7d 对称性。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,组装途径受静电相互作用控制,控制离子强度或突变特定残基可以导致直接从细菌裂解物中形成高质量、免疫原性的 VLP。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现对 HPV 疫苗 的 VLP 生产具有影响,因为它们表明,仔细控制盐浓度和靶向 突变 可以提高 VLP 的质量,而无需拆卸和重新组装步骤。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究基于计算模型和实验验证,在充分捕捉体内组装过程的复杂性方面可能存在局限性。由于依赖模拟且缺乏直接的临床结果,证据是中等的。
