papers.full_text: BackgroundOropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC) has undergone substantial epidemiological and clinical changes, with an increasing proportion of human papillomavirus (HPV)-associated tumours and declining tobacco exposure. We investigated temporal changes in patient characteristics, HPV/p16 status, treatment patterns, and survival among patients with OPSCC in Denmark.MethodsPatients with OPSCC were identified from the Copenhagen Oropharyngeal Cancer Database (2000–2023) and the Danish National Patient Cancer Registry (DCR; 1980–2021). The Copenhagen database provided detailed clinical and pathological data, including HPV/p16 status, while the DCR enabled assessment of long-term survival trends. Temporal changes were evaluated across diagnostic periods. Overall survival, relative survival, and restricted mean survival time were estimated.ResultsAmong 3,631 OPSCC patients in the Copenhagen database, median age at diagnosis increased from 59 years in 2000–2005 to 64 years in 2018–2023 (p<0.001). The proportion of HPV+/p16+ patients increased significantly from 43.5% in 2000–2005 to 62.8% in 2018-2023. The proportion of never smokers also increased from 0.5% to 23.5%, while ≥20 pack-years decreased from 73.2% to 52.1% (p<0.001). Treatment patterns changed substantially, with radiotherapy alone decreasing from 87.6% to 27.9% and chemoradiotherapy increasing from 1.6% to 46.3%. Among 9,379 patients in the DCR, five-year relative survival increased from 31.8% in 1980–1984 to 70.1% in 2015-2019. Among HPV+/p16+ patients, five-year overall survival increased from 63.1% in 2000–2005 to 83.7% in 2018–2023.ConclusionIn Denmark, OPSCC has undergone substantial epidemiological and therapeutic changes accompanied by marked improvements in survival, including among HPV+/p16+ patients. MethodStudy designThis study was designed as a retrospective registry-based cohort study with an additional matched population-comparator analysis.ParticipantsWe included patients diagnosed with oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC) in Denmark. Data were obtained from two complementary sources: the Copenhagen Oropharyngeal Cancer Database and the Danish National Patient Cancer Registry (DCR). The Copenhagen Oropharyngeal Cancer Database contains patients diagnosed with OPSCC within the Eastern Danish healthcare region and covers the period from 2000 to 2023. The database is updated at three-year intervals and covers approximately half of the Danish population.To extend the study period and identify patients diagnosed prior to establishment of the Copenhagen database, data from the DCR were used for patients diagnosed between 1980 and 2021.Using data from the Danish Civil Registration System, each patient with OPSCC identified in the DCR was matched to 10 population controls based on age, sex, and calendar year of diagnosis. Controls were selected from the Danish general population and were eligible for matching if they were alive and had not been diagnosed with head and neck cancer before the index date. The index date for each control was defined as the corresponding calendar year of diagnosis of OPSCC in the matched patient. Matching was performed without replacement, such that each control could be assigned to only one patient. Patients for whom 10 eligible controls could not be identified were excluded from the matched analysis. Follow-up for patients and matched controls was calculated from the index date until death, emigration, or the end of the study period, whichever occurred first.Data sourcesThe Copenhagen Oropharyngeal Cancer Database is based on data from the Danish Pathology Registry and the Danish Head and Neck Cancer Group (DAHANCA) database and is supplemented with information extracted from electronic health records (Epic Systems). Patients were identified using their unique Danish personal identification number. Clinical and pathological data were collected in a Research Electronic Data Capture (REDCap) database at Copenhagen University Hospital – Rigshospitalet, Denmark.Patients with biopsy-confirmed OPSCC diagnosed in Eastern Denmark between January 1, 2000, and December 31, 2023, were identified from the DAHANCA database and the Danish Pathology Data Registry. The DAHANCA database prospectively records clinical characteristics of patients with head and neck cancer, while the Danish Pathology Data Registry is a mandatory nationwide registry containing information on tissue samples collected from patients treated in Denmark. Only the first occurring OPSCC were included in this study. Patients were followed from the date of diagnosis (the date of the first biopsy) until death or the end of the follow-up period. Patients who were alive at the last day of follow-up (1/11-24) were censored on that date.For patients diagnosed from 2000 onwards, tumour stage was retrospectively classified according to the UICC 8th edition staging system for p16-positive OPSCC. The available UICC 7th edition N categories were converted as follows: N0 remained N0, N1 remained N1, N2a and N2b were recoded as N1, N2c as N2, and N3 remained N3. For T classification, T4a and T4b were combined into T4. The resulting T and N categories were then used to assign UICC 8th edition stage groups according to the following scheme: stage I for T1–2N0–1, stage II for T1–3N2 and T3N0–1, and stage III for T1–3N3 and all T4 tumours.p16 testingp16 expression was assessed by immunohistochemistry (IHC) using the Ventana Benchmark Ultra autostainer and the p16 monoclonal antibody E6H4 with CC1 pretreatment (Roche, Tucson, AZ, USA) throughout the study period. For tumours diagnosed between 2018 and 2023, the OptiView detection kit was used and tumours were considered p16-positive when >70% of tumour cells showed cytoplasmic and/or nuclear staining. Before 2018, the UltraView detection kit was used and the cutoff for p16 positivity was >75% of tumour cells showing cytoplasmic and nuclear staining.HPV testingFormalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tumour tissue was used for HPV DNA extraction and asseessment. Different methods were used for HPV DNA evaluation during the study period. For tumours diagnosed between 2021 and 2023 HPV DNA was detected using the VisionArray HPV Chip 1.0 system (ZytoVision, Bremerhaven, Germany), which detects 41 clinically relevant HPV genotypes. The assay was performed according to the manufacturer’s instructions as previously described (2). Samples with discordant HPV and p16 results were retested. For tumours diagnosed between 2018 and 2020, HPV DNA was detected using either a broad-spectrum GP5+/6+ polymerase chain reaction (PCR) assay or the VisionArray HPV Chip 1.0. For the GP5+/6+ PCR assay, DNA quality was confirmed using a glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate dehydrogenase (GAPDH) control, and samples positive for GP5+/6+ and GAPDH were classified as HPV-positive. The method has previously been described (5). Before 2018, HPV DNA was detected using the GP5+/6+ PCR assay. DNA quality was assessed using GAPDH PCR. HPV genotyping was performed by sequencing of GP5+/6+ amplicons using next-generation sequencing, as previously described (9).The DCR includes information on cancer diagnoses, including International Classification of Disease 10 revision (ICD-10) codes, MORPHO3 codes, treatment, and survival outcomes. Patients were identified using relevant ICD-10 diagnosis codes and histological information. The included ICD-10 codes were DC01, DC01.9, DC02.4, DC05.1, DC05.2, DC09, DC09.0–DC09.9, DC10.0, DC10.2, DC10.3, DC10.8, and DC10.9. Histologically, cases were classified as squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) and thus included based on the following MORPH3 codes: 80303, 80313, 80323, 80333, 80513, 80523, 80703, 80709, 80713, 80719, 80723, 80733, 80743, 80753, 80763, 80823, 80829, 80833, 80843, 80853, 80863, 81213, 81233, 82303, 82309, and 85603. Patients were included if they were registered with an OPSCC in the DCR between 1/1–1980 and 31/12-2020. Only the first occurring OPSCC were included in the study. Patients were followed from the date of diagnosis until death or the end of the follow-up period. Patients who were alive at the last day of follow-up (1/1-24) were censored on that date.The two data sources served complementary purposes: the DCR enabled analyses covering a longer historical period, whereas the Copenhagen Oropharyngeal Cancer Database provided more detailed clinical and pathological data, including HPV and p16 status. The specific data source used for each analysis is indicated in the corresponding tables and figures.Study sizeFrom the Copenhagen Oropharyngeal Cancer Database, a total of 3,631 patients were included.A total of 9,057 patients with OPSCC were identified in the DCR. One patient was lost to follow-up and was excluded from the analysis, resulting in a total of 9,056 patients. Eighteen patients emigrated from Denmark during follow-up and were censored at the date of emigration.For the matched analysis, each patient was matched with 10 population controls based on age, sex, and year of diagnosis. Seven patients could not be assigned eligible controls and were therefore excluded from the matched analysis, leaving 9,049 patients for the matched analysis. Of these, eight controls were excluded because they died before the matching date. In total, 90,482 controls were included in the matched analysis.Study outcomesThe primary objective was to characterise temporal changes in the clinical characteristics of patients with OPSCC in parallel with the increasing proportion of HPV-associated disease. The primary outcomes were temporal changes in HPV/p16 status, patient characteristics, tumour stage, and treatment modality. Secondary outcomes included temporal changes in relative survival, overall survival, long-term survival, and survival compared with matched population controls.For temporal analyses, the study periods were divided into approximately equal intervals. For data from the Copenhagen database, the study period was divided into four periods: 2000–2005, 2006–2011, 2012–2017, and 2018–2023. For data from the DCR, the study period was divided into nine periods: 1980–1984, 1985–1989, 1990–1994, 1995–1999, 2000–2004, 2005–2009, 2010–2014, 2015–2019, and 2020–2021 thereby extending the analysis to include the full available study period.Statistical analysisDescriptive statistics were used to summarize the study population and tumour characteristics. Categorical variables were presented as numbers and percentages, while continuous variables were summarized using appropriate measures of central tendency and dispersion.Overall survivalOverall survival was estimated using the Kaplan–Meier method, with time calculated from the date of OPSCC diagnosis to the date of death or last available follow-up. Patients who were alive at the end of follow-up were censored at their last known date of follow-up. Kaplan–Meier curves were generated to illustrate overall survival across diagnostic periods, and differences between survival curves were assessed using the log-rank test.Long-term survivalTo assess changes in long-term survival, patients were grouped according to diagnostic period, and Kaplan–Meier estimates of overall survival at 5, 10, and 15 years were calculated. For each survival interval, only patients with sufficient potential follow-up were included. Given follow-up through 2024 (last day of follow-up 1 January 2024), patients diagnosed after 2018, 2013, and 2008 were excluded from the 5-, 10-, and 15-year analyses, respectively. Overall survival at each time point was estimated using the Kaplan–Meier method, with 95% confidence intervals.Relative survivalRelative survival was estimated using data from the DCR to assess survival among patients with OPSCC relative to the expected survival in the general Danish population. Expected survival was derived from Danish population life tables obtained from Statistics Denmark and stratified by age, sex, and calendar year. The relative survival rate was calculated as the ratio of observed to expected survival in Denmark, adjusted for age, sex, and calendar year, using the R package ‘relsurv’. Relative survival curves were estimated using the Ederer II method, with expected survival determined from the population life tables according to age, sex, and calendar year.Survival compared with matched controlsRestricted mean survival time (RMST) was used to quantify differences in survival between patients with OPSCC and matched controls over predefined follow-up periods. This measure represents the expected time alive within a specified follow-up horizon (10). Estimates were obtained at 5, 10, and 15 years after diagnosis for both groups, and the between-group difference in RMST was calculated with corresponding 95% confidence intervals. Thus, the difference in RMST represents the difference in accumulated survival time between patients with OPSCC and their matched controls within each specified time horizon.All statistical analyses were performed using RStudio (version 2025.05.1). Statistical significance was defined as a two-sided P value ≤0.05.ResultsA total of 3,631 patients with OPSCC were included from the Copenhagen database. The median age at diagnosis increased significantly over time, from 59 years (IQR, 52.8–66.0) in 2000–2005 to 64 years (IQR, 57–71) in 2018–2023 (p<0.001). The sex distribution remained stable, with men accounting for approximately 71–74% of patients across all periods (p=0.6) (Table 1). A marked shift in HPV/p16 status was observed over time (p<0.001). The proportion of HPV+/p16+ tumours increased from 43.5% in 2000–2005 to 62.8% in 2018–2023, while the proportion of HPV−/p16− tumours decreased from 40.7% to 24.8%. The proportions of both HPV−/p16+ and HPV+/p16− tumours also decreased over time. The distribution of HPV/p16 status varied by age and diagnosis period (Figure 1). Across all age groups, HPV+/p16+ tumors increased over time, while HPV−/p16− tumors decreased. The increase was most pronounced among patients aged <50 years, with HPV+/p16+ tumors rising from approximately 50% in 2000–2005 to 90% in 2018–2023, compared with an increase from 30% to 60% among full_text_sections.abstract: BackgroundOropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC) has undergone substantial epidemiological and clinical changes, with an increasing proportion of human papillomavirus (HPV)-associated tumours and declining tobacco exposure. We investigated temporal changes in patient characteristics, HPV/p16 status, treatment patterns, and survival among patients with OPSCC in Denmark.MethodsPatients with OPSCC were identified from the Copenhagen Oropharyngeal Cancer Database (2000–2023) and the Danish National Patient Cancer Registry (DCR; 1980–2021). The Copenhagen database provided detailed clinical and pathological data, including HPV/p16 status, while the DCR enabled assessment of long-term survival trends. Temporal changes were evaluated across diagnostic periods. Overall survival, relative survival, and restricted mean survival time were estimated.ResultsAmong 3,631 OPSCC patients in the Copenhagen database, median age at diagnosis increased from 59 years in 2000–2005 to 64 years in 2018–2023 (p<0.001). The proportion of HPV+/p16+ patients increased significantly from 43.5% in 2000–2005 to 62.8% in 2018-2023. The proportion of never smokers also increased from 0.5% to 23.5%, while ≥20 pack-years decreased from 73.2% to 52.1% (p<0.001). Treatment patterns changed substantially, with radiotherapy alone decreasing from 87.6% to 27.9% and chemoradiotherapy increasing from 1.6% to 46.3%. Among 9,379 patients in the DCR, five-year relative survival increased from 31.8% in 1980–1984 to 70.1% in 2015-2019. Among HPV+/p16+ patients, five-year overall survival increased from 63.1% in 2000–2005 to 83.7% in 2018–2023.ConclusionIn Denmark, OPSCC has undergone substantial epidemiological and therapeutic changes accompanied by marked improvements in survival, including among HPV+/p16+ patients.
full_text_sections.methods: MethodStudy designThis study was designed as a retrospective registry-based cohort study with an additional matched population-comparator analysis.ParticipantsWe included patients diagnosed with oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC) in Denmark. Data were obtained from two complementary sources: the Copenhagen Oropharyngeal Cancer Database and the Danish National Patient Cancer Registry (DCR). The Copenhagen Oropharyngeal Cancer Database contains patients diagnosed with OPSCC within the Eastern Danish healthcare region and covers the period from 2000 to 2023. The database is updated at three-year intervals and covers approximately half of the Danish population.To extend the study period and identify patients diagnosed prior to establishment of the Copenhagen database, data from the DCR were used for patients diagnosed between 1980 and 2021.Using data from the Danish Civil Registration System, each patient with OPSCC identified in the DCR was matched to 10 population controls based on age, sex, and calendar year of diagnosis. Controls were selected from the Danish general population and were eligible for matching if they were alive and had not been diagnosed with head and neck cancer before the index date. The index date for each control was defined as the corresponding calendar year of diagnosis of OPSCC in the matched patient. Matching was performed without replacement, such that each control could be assigned to only one patient. Patients for whom 10 eligible controls could not be identified were excluded from the matched analysis. Follow-up for patients and matched controls was calculated from the index date until death, emigration, or the end of the study period, whichever occurred first.Data sourcesThe Copenhagen Oropharyngeal Cancer Database is based on data from the Danish Pathology Registry and the Danish Head and Neck Cancer Group (DAHANCA) database and is supplemented with information extracted from electronic health records (Epic Systems). Patients were identified using their unique Danish personal identification number. Clinical and pathological data were collected in a Research Electronic Data Capture (REDCap) database at Copenhagen University Hospital – Rigshospitalet, Denmark.Patients with biopsy-confirmed OPSCC diagnosed in Eastern Denmark between January 1, 2000, and December 31, 2023, were identified from the DAHANCA database and the Danish Pathology Data Registry. The DAHANCA database prospectively records clinical characteristics of patients with head and neck cancer, while the Danish Pathology Data Registry is a mandatory nationwide registry containing information on tissue samples collected from patients treated in Denmark. Only the first occurring OPSCC were included in this study. Patients were followed from the date of diagnosis (the date of the first biopsy) until death or the end of the follow-up period. Patients who were alive at the last day of follow-up (1/11-24) were censored on that date.For patients diagnosed from 2000 onwards, tumour stage was retrospectively classified according to the UICC 8th edition staging system for p16-positive OPSCC. The available UICC 7th edition N categories were converted as follows: N0 remained N0, N1 remained N1, N2a and N2b were recoded as N1, N2c as N2, and N3 remained N3. For T classification, T4a and T4b were combined into T4. The resulting T and N categories were then used to assign UICC 8th edition stage groups according to the following scheme: stage I for T1–2N0–1, stage II for T1–3N2 and T3N0–1, and stage III for T1–3N3 and all T4 tumours.p16 testingp16 expression was assessed by immunohistochemistry (IHC) using the Ventana Benchmark Ultra autostainer and the p16 monoclonal antibody E6H4 with CC1 pretreatment (Roche, Tucson, AZ, USA) throughout the study period. For tumours diagnosed between 2018 and 2023, the OptiView detection kit was used and tumours were considered p16-positive when >70% of tumour cells showed cytoplasmic and/or nuclear staining. Before 2018, the UltraView detection kit was used and the cutoff for p16 positivity was >75% of tumour cells showing cytoplasmic and nuclear staining.HPV testingFormalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tumour tissue was used for HPV DNA extraction and asseessment. Different methods were used for HPV DNA evaluation during the study period. For tumours diagnosed between 2021 and 2023 HPV DNA was detected using the VisionArray HPV Chip 1.0 system (ZytoVision, Bremerhaven, Germany), which detects 41 clinically relevant HPV genotypes. The assay was performed according to the manufacturer’s instructions as previously described (2). Samples with discordant HPV and p16 results were retested. For tumours diagnosed between 2018 and 2020, HPV DNA was detected using either a broad-spectrum GP5+/6+ polymerase chain reaction (PCR) assay or the VisionArray HPV Chip 1.0. For the GP5+/6+ PCR assay, DNA quality was confirmed using a glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate dehydrogenase (GAPDH) control, and samples positive for GP5+/6+ and GAPDH were classified as HPV-positive. The method has previously been described (5). Before 2018, HPV DNA was detected using the GP5+/6+ PCR assay. DNA quality was assessed using GAPDH PCR. Patients were included if they were registered with an OPSCC in the DCR between 1/1–1980 and 31/12-2020. Only the first occurring OPSCC were included in the study. Patients were followed from the date of diagnosis until death or the end of the follow-up period. Patients who were alive at the last day of follow-up (1/1-24) were censored on that date.The two data sources served complementary purposes: the DCR enabled analyses covering a longer historical period, whereas the Copenhagen Oropharyngeal Cancer Database provided more detailed clinical and pathological data, including HPV and p16 status. One patient was lost to follow-up and was excluded from the analysis, resulting in a total of 9,056 patients. Eighteen patients emigrated from Denmark during follow-up and were censored at the date of emigration.For the matched analysis, each patient was matched with 10 population controls based on age, sex, and year of diagnosis. Seven patients could not be assigned eligible controls and were therefore excluded from the matched analysis, leaving 9,049 patients for the matched analysis. Of these, eight controls were excluded because they died before the matching date. In total, 90,482 controls were included in the matched analysis.Study outcomesThe primary objective was to characterise temporal changes in the clinical characteristics of patients with OPSCC in parallel with the increasing proportion of HPV-associated disease. The primary outcomes were temporal changes in HPV/p16 status, patient characteristics, tumour stage, and treatment modality. full_text_sections.discussion: DiscussionIn this study, we observed substantial changes in the epidemiology, treatment, and survival of patients with OPSCC over time.Treatment patterns changed considerably during the study period, with radiotherapy alone becoming less common and combined treatment modality increasing. These changes may reflect advances in the multidisciplinary management of OPSCC, including centralisation of treatment decisions in multidisciplinary tumour boards, refinement of positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT)-based staging, and the introduction of transoral robotic surgery as a treatment option for selected early-stage tumours (11), although this study did not directly evaluate the drivers of these treatment shifts. Notably, despite the favourable prognosis of HPV+/p16+ OPSCC, treatment de-intensification has not been established as standard practice. Randomised trials evaluating reduced-intensity treatment in this subgroup, including the De-ESCALaTE HPV and Radiation Therapy Oncology Group (RTOG) 1016 trials, failed to demonstrate non-inferiority of cetuximab-based regimens compared with cisplatin-based chemoradiotherapy, and de-escalation therefore remains investigational inside clinical trials (12). This is consistent with continued reliance on combined-modality treatment, rather than de-escalated single-modality regimens, despite the growing proportion of HPV+/p16+ tumours observed in our cohort.Survival improved substantially over the study period. In the DCR cohort, five-year relative survival increased from 31.9% in patients diagnosed in 1980–1984 to 70.1% in those diagnosed in 2015–2019. A similar improvement was observed among HPV+/p16+ patients based on data from the Copenhagen Database, for whom five-year overall survival increased from 63.1% in 2000–2005 to 83.7% in 2018–2023. This improvement is consistent with the established prognostic significance of HPV status first demonstrated by Ang et al. (13), and extends findings from previous Danish nationwide studies reporting improving OPSCC survival over time (5, 8). Importantly, survival also improved within the HPV+/p16+ subgroup, indicating that the increasing proportion of HPV-driven tumours alone does not fully account for the observed population-level improvement in survival. Possible explanations for the remaining improvement include refinements in staging accuracy, changes in patient selection, and improvements in treatment delivery over time. The introduction of HPV-specific staging in the eighth edition of the AJCC/UICC TNM classification during the study period should be considered when interpreting temporal comparisons of stage-stratified outcomes. However, as patients diagnosed from 2000 onwards were retrospectively classified according to UICC 8 using the available UICC 7 T and N categories, differences in stage distribution cannot be attributed solely to the change in staging system. The observed temporal changes may reflect underlying differences in tumour biology and disease presentation, including the increasing proportion of HPV/p16-positive OPSCC. Concurrently, declining tobacco exposure in the general population is likely to have contributed independently to the changing tumour biology (2, 14, 15).The present study builds on previous Danish studies of OPSCC, including the Copenhagen cohort reported by Michaelsen et al. (2) and the nationwide Danish Cancer Registry study by Jakobsen et al (8). While there is substantial cohort overlap, the present study extends these findings by providing a broader longitudinal assessment of clinical characteristics, tumour stage, and treatment patterns, with particular emphasis on long-term survival. The increasing proportion of long-term survivors further demonstrates the substantial improvement in prognosis. However, the comparison with matched population controls showed that patients with OPSCC continued to experience a substantial survival deficit, which increased with longer follow-up. This finding highlighting that improved cancer survival does not necessarily translate into survival comparable to that of the general population. These findings emphasise the growing population of long-term OPSCC survivors and the increasing importance of survivorship and management of late treatment-related effects, including dysphagia, xerostomia, and other functional sequelae of chemoradiotherapy, which can persist for years after treatment completion and substantially affect quality of life (16). This underscores the need for structured, long-term survivorship programmes as an increasing share of the OPSCC population moves from active treatment into extended follow-up.A key strength of this study is the use of two complementary data sources. The evaluation of survival trends over more than four decades was enabled by the DCR, while the Copenhagen database provided detailed clinical and pathological information, including HPV/p16 status. Limitations include limited availability of HPV/p16 data in the DCR, and shorter follow-up in the most recent cohorts. Additionally, changes in staging classification during the study period may limit direct comparability of stage-specific outcomes across diagnostic periods. Further, HPV DNA and p16 status were assessed using different methods and protocols over the study period, including different HPV DNA assays and p16 detection kits and positivity thresholds, which may have introduced some degree of methodological heterogeneity in the classification of HPV/p16 status. Lastly, the completeness of smoking data varied over the study period, and differences in the ascertainment or recording of smoking status over time may have contributed to the observed temporal increase in the proportion of never-smokers. Therefore, this finding should be interpreted with consideration of potential temporal ascertainment bias.In conclusion, OPSCC in Denmark has undergone substantial epidemiological and therapeutic changes, accompanied by marked improvements in both short- and long-term survival. These improvements were also evident among HPV+/p16+ patients, underscoring continued progress in the management of OPSCC. Importantly, the present study demonstrates that these improvements extend to long-term survival and provides insight into survival relative to the Danish general population.

papers.title_original: Changing epidemiology and survival of HPV-associated oropharyngeal cancer in Denmark: four decades of population-based data

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate temporal changes in patient characteristics, HPV/p16 status, treatment patterns, and survival among patients with HPV-associated oropharyngeal cancer (OPSCC) in Denmark.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Patients with biopsy-confirmed OPSCC diagnosed in Eastern Denmark between January 1, 2000, and December 31, 2023, were identified from the DAHANCA database and the Danish National Patient Cancer Registry (DCR). The two data sources served complementary purposes: the DCR enabled analyses covering a longer historical period, whereas the Copenhagen Oropharyngeal Cancer Database provided more detailed clinical and pathological data, including HPV and p16 status.
analysis.methods: Clinical and pathological data were collected in a Research Electronic Data Capture (REDCap) database. For tumours diagnosed between 2018 and 2020, HPV DNA was detected using either a broad-spectrum GP5+/6+ polymerase chain reaction (PCR) assay or the VisionArray HPV Chip 1.0. DNA quality was confirmed using a glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate dehydrogenase (GAPDH) control, and samples positive for GP5+/6+ and GAPDH were classified as HPV-positive.
analysis.main_results: Among 3,631 OPSCC patients in the Copenhagen database, median age at diagnosis increased from 59 years in 2000–2005 to 64 years in 2018–2023 (p<0.001). The proportion of HPV+/p16+ patients increased significantly from 43.5% in 2000–2005 to 62.8% in 2018–2023. The proportion of never smokers increased from 0.5% to 23.1%, while the proportion of patients with ≥20 pack-years decreased from 62.4% to 51.7%. Five-year relative survival increased from 31.8% in 1980–1984 to 70.1% in 2015-2019 among 9,379 patients in the DCR. Among HPV+/p16+ patients, five-year overall survival increased from 63.1% in 2000–2005 to 83.7% in 2018–2023.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that OPSCC has undergone substantial epidemiological and therapeutic changes accompanied by marked improvements in survival, including among HPV+/p16+ patients. This finding highlights a significant shift in the disease's characteristics and treatment outcomes over time.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform surveillance and diagnostic strategies for HPV-associated oropharyngeal cancer, as well as guide treatment approaches and risk assessment for patients with varying HPV/p16 statuses.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's evidence is moderate, as it relies on registry data and does not include direct causal relationships or detailed laboratory procedures. The use of different detection kits for p16 and HPV status over time may introduce variability in results.

analysis.summary_en: This study examines the changing epidemiology and survival of HPV-associated oropharyngeal cancer (OPSCC) in Denmark over four decades. It reports a significant increase in the proportion of HPV+/p16+ patients, a rise in median age at diagnosis, and a marked improvement in survival rates, particularly among HPV+/p16+ individuals. The study highlights shifts in smoking and alcohol patterns, as well as treatment modalities, over time. While the findings suggest substantial changes in disease characteristics and outcomes, the evidence is moderate due to reliance on registry data and potential variability in HPV/p16 detection methods. The results have implications for surveillance, diagnosis, and treatment strategies for HPV-associated OPSCC, emphasizing the need for updated approaches in clinical and public health settings.

papers.source_body_en: MethodStudy designThis study was designed as a retrospective registry-based cohort study with an additional matched population-comparator analysis.ParticipantsWe included patients diagnosed with oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC) in Denmark. The database is updated at three-year intervals and covers approximately half of the Danish population.To extend the study period and identify patients diagnosed prior to establishment of the Copenhagen database, data from the DCR were used for patients diagnosed between 1980 and 2021.Using data from the Danish Civil Registration System, each patient with OPSCC identified in the DCR was matched to 10 population controls based on age, sex, and calendar year of diagnosis. Follow-up for patients and matched controls was calculated from the index date until death, emigration, or the end of the study period, whichever occurred first.Data sourcesThe Copenhagen Oropharyngeal Cancer Database is based on data from the Danish Pathology Registry and the Danish Head and Neck Cancer Group (DAHANCA) database and is supplemented with information extracted from electronic health records (Epic Systems). Only the first occurring OPSCC were included in this study. papers.full_text: Abstract Evidence comparing cervical cancer screening strategies that combine artificial intelligence-assisted liquid-based cytology (AI-LBC) and high-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) testing in large-scale populations is limited. This study includes 284,002 women who underwent AI-LBC and HR-HPV genotyping in community-based screening in Wuhan, China. We evaluate the performance of nine hypothesized screening strategies in detecting cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 2 or worse (CIN2+) and their colposcopy referral rates. After correcting for verification bias, HR-HPV testing alone (Strategy 4) demonstrates higher sensitivity (94.93% vs. 83.88%) and a higher Youden’s index (0.864 vs. 0.789) than AI-LBC alone (Strategy 1), but requires a higher referral rate (9.05% vs. 5.49%). Among the triage-based strategies, Strategy 3 (AI-LBC with reflex HR-HPV) achieves a sensitivity of 82.90%, a referral rate of 2.67%, and a Youden’s index of 0.807. HR-HPV genotyping with reflex AI-LBC (Strategy 7) demonstrates a sensitivity of 92.68%, a Youden’s index of 0.899, and a referral rate of 3.34%. analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to evaluate the performance of cervical cancer screening strategies combining artificial intelligence-assisted liquid-based cytology (AI-LBC) and high-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) testing, as evidence comparing these strategies in large-scale populations is limited.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved 284,002 women who underwent AI-LBC and HR-HPV genotyping in community-based cervical cancer screening in Wuhan, China, between 2019 and 2023.
analysis.methods: The researchers evaluated nine hypothesized screening strategies for detecting cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 2 or worse (CIN2+) and their colposcopy referral rates, using HR-HPV genotyping and AI-LBC as the primary assays, with adjustments for verification bias.
analysis.main_results: HR-HPV testing alone (Strategy 4) showed higher sensitivity (94.93%) and Youden’s index (0.864) than AI-LBC alone (Strategy 1), but required a higher referral rate (9.05%). Co-testing of AI-LBC and HR-HPV genotyping (Strategy 9) achieved the highest Youden’s index (0.932), with a sensitivity of 96.37% and a referral rate of 3.70%.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that AI-LBC performs well as a standalone screening method, triage tool, or component of a co-testing strategy, highlighting its potential utility in cervical cancer screening.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results may inform the selection of screening strategies in settings where HR-HPV genotyping is available, balancing detection performance with referral burden for effective cervical cancer prevention.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's design may be limited by potential verification bias, and the results are specific to the Chinese population, which may affect generalisability. The evidence is moderate in strength due to these limitations.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluates nine cervical cancer screening strategies combining artificial intelligence-assisted liquid-based cytology (AI-LBC) and high-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) testing in 284,002 women in Wuhan, China. The main results show that HR-HPV testing alone has higher sensitivity and Youden’s index than AI-LBC alone, but requires a higher referral rate. Co-testing of AI-LBC and HR-HPV achieves the highest Youden’s index, with high sensitivity and moderate referral rate. The authors interpret these findings as indicating AI-LBC's effectiveness as a standalone method or triage tool. The study's implications suggest that HR-HPV genotyping with reflex AI-LBC or co-testing may be preferable in settings where HR-HPV is available, depending on the balance between detection performance and referral burden. However, the study's design may be limited by verification bias, and its results may not be generalizable beyond the Chinese population. The evidence is moderate in strength due to these limitations.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在评估结合人工智能辅助液基细胞学 (AI-LBC) 和高风险 人乳头瘤病毒 (HR-HPV) 检测的 宫颈癌 筛查策略的性能,因为在大规模人群中比较这些策略的证据有限。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究涉及 2019 年至 2023 年间在中国武汉基于社区的 宫颈癌 筛查中接受 AI-LBC 和 HR-HPV 基因分型的 284,002 名女性。
elements_zh.methods: 研究人员使用 HR-HPV 基因分型和 AI-LBC 作为主要检测方法,评估了九种假设的检测 2 级或更严重宫颈上皮内瘤变 (CIN2+) 的筛查策略及其阴道镜转诊率,并根据验证偏差进行了调整。
elements_zh.main_results: 单独的 HR-HPV 检测(策略 4)比单独的 AI-LBC(策略 1)显示出更高的敏感性(94.93%)和 Youden 指数(0.864),但需要更高的转诊率(9.05%)。AI-LBC 和 HR-HPV 基因分型联合检测(策略 9)取得了最高的 Youden 指数(0.932),敏感性为 96.37%,转诊率为 3.70%。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,AI-LBC 作为独立的筛查方法、分类工具或联合测试策略的组成部分表现良好,突出了其在 宫颈癌 筛查中的潜在效用。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果可以为可进行 HR-HPV 基因分型的环境中筛查策略的选择提供参考,平衡检测性能与转诊负担,以实现有效的 宫颈癌 预防。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的设计可能受到潜在验证偏差的限制,并且结果仅针对中国人群,这可能会影响普遍性。由于这些限制,证据的强度中等。

papers.title: Prevalence and genotype distribution of cervical HPV infection among women in Tehran: a cross-sectional molecular study
papers.abstract: Background Persistent infection with carcinogenic human papillomavirus (HPV) types is the main cause of cervical cancer. HPV genotype surveillance provides important epidemiological information for cervical cancer prevention.Methods A cross-sectional study was conducted in 2025 among 220 women attending hospitals and gynecology outpatient clinics in Tehran. Cervical samples collected in liquid-based cytology (LBC) medium were tested for HPV genotypes using multiplex real-time PCR. Cytology results were available for 134 participants.Results HPV DNA was detected in 52/220 women (23.6%). The most frequently detected genotypes among HPV-positive women were HPV66 (11/52, 21.2%), HPV16 (9/52, 17.3%), and HPV68 (7/52, 13.5%). Among participants with available cytology, HPV positivity was detected in 28/107 (26.2%) women with normal cytology and 4/27 (14.8%) with abnormal cytology, with no significant difference. Marital status was associated with HPV positivity in univariable analysis.Conclusion This study provides descriptive data on HPV prevalence and genotype distribution in a clinically selected population in Tehran. Further population-based studies with systematic cytological and histopathological follow-up are needed to better define HPV-related cervical cancer prevention strategies in Iran.

papers.title: Productive or Transforming? How Epithelial Compartmentalization of HPV DNA and E6/E7 Transcripts Shapes Cervical Screening Assay Performance.
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT The human papillomavirus (HPV) life cycle is linked to epithelial cell differentiation, with viral genome amplification, E6/E7 transcription, and virion assembly spatially compartmentalized within the cervical epithelium. This organization is disrupted in transforming lesions. These fundamental observations determine what ‘bulk’ nucleic acid amplification tests (NAATs) of cervical exfoliates allow us to establish. DNA‐based assays sensitively report high‐risk HPV genome presence, which includes transient infections and virus particles. RNA‐based assays target the E6/E7 transcripts in transcriptionally active disease, which accounts for their slightly higher clinical specificity for high‐grade squamous intraepithelial lesions. No single assay defines both viral presence and disease significance, however. Cytology, p16/Ki‐67 dual stain, extended genotyping and host‐cell methylation interrogate complementary axes of risk with strong biological rationale. The loss of spatial information that limits bulk NAAT approaches matters most in mixed‐grade lesions and immunocompromised populations. Emerging spatial methods, AI‐assisted cytology and cervical cell‐lifts offer recovery of biological resolution.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study investigates how the spatial compartmentalization of HPV DNA and E6/E7 transcripts within cervical epithelial cells influences the performance of cervical screening assays. It addresses the need to understand the limitations of current bulk nucleic acid amplification tests (NAATs) in distinguishing between viral presence and disease significance.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study is a review of existing literature and observations on the organization of HPV within cervical epithelium, focusing on human papillomavirus (HPV) and its association with cervical intraepithelial neoplasia, HPV-associated cervical cancer, and other HPV-related diseases. It examines the disruption of this organization in transforming lesions.
analysis.methods: The study employs a combination of cytology, p16/Ki-67 dual stain, extended genotyping, and host-cell methylation to interrogate complementary axes of risk. These methods are grounded in strong biological rationale and aim to recover spatial information lost in bulk NAAT approaches.
analysis.main_results: DNA-based assays sensitively report the presence of high-risk HPV genomes, including transient infections and virus particles, while RNA-based assays target E6/E7 transcripts in transcriptionally active disease, which contributes to their slightly higher clinical specificity for high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that the loss of spatial information in bulk NAAT approaches is most significant in mixed-grade lesions and immunocompromised populations. They highlight the novelty of emerging spatial methods, AI-assisted cytology, and cervical cell-lifts as potential solutions to recover biological resolution.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform the development of more accurate cervical screening assays that can distinguish between viral presence and disease significance, particularly in complex cases such as mixed-grade lesions and immunocompromised individuals.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on abstract-only evidence and the lack of detailed statistical analyses. The evidence strength is moderate, as the conclusions are based on existing observations and biological rationale rather than new experimental data.

analysis.summary_en: This study explores how the spatial compartmentalization of human papillomavirus (HPV) DNA and E6/E7 transcripts within cervical epithelial cells affects the performance of cervical screening assays. It highlights that DNA-based assays detect HPV genome presence, including transient infections, while RNA-based assays target transcriptionally active disease, offering slightly higher specificity for high-grade lesions. The authors emphasize the importance of spatial information in mixed-grade and immunocompromised cases, suggesting that emerging methods like AI-assisted cytology and cervical cell-lifts may improve diagnostic accuracy. The study is a review based on existing literature and biological rationale, with moderate evidence strength due to its abstract-only nature and lack of detailed statistical analyses.

papers.title: Towards a sequential microbiome therapy for HPV-associated cervicovaginal dysbiosis.
papers.abstract: Abstract Persistent high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) infections are the principal cause of cervical cancer, and are increasingly associated with ecological instability of the cervicovaginal microbiome. Multiomics studies indicate that hrHPV persistence is linked to reduced Lactobacillus dominance, increased anaerobic taxa, and metabolic alterations that may compromise epithelial integrity and antiviral immunity. In this Perspective article, we introduce a sequential microbiome therapy (SMT) framework designed to restore cervicovaginal ecological balance and support viral clearance. SMT is a two-phase, strain-resolved strategy. The first phase targets dysbiotic communities using antimicrobials, biofilm-disrupting or microbiota-modulating approaches to create a window for ecological reset. The second phase introduces health-associated Lactobacillus species selected for their acidification capacity, competitive fitness, and ability to stabilize the mucosal environment. We outline the ecological principles underpinning SMT and discuss its development as a potentially scalable microbiome-directed strategy for restoring cervicovaginal health and managing hrHPV-associated disease within existing cervical cancer prevention frameworks.

analysis.summary_en: This review introduces a sequential microbiome therapy (SMT) framework for restoring cervicovaginal ecological balance and supporting viral clearance in high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) infections. The evidence highlights that hrHPV persistence is associated with reduced Lactobacillus dominance, increased anaerobic taxa, and metabolic changes that may impair epithelial integrity and antiviral immunity. The SMT approach involves two phases: the first targets dysbiotic communities using antimicrobials, biofilm-disrupting agents, or microbiota-modulating strategies to reset the microbiome, while the second phase introduces health-associated Lactobacillus species with specific traits to stabilize the mucosal environment. The review outlines the ecological principles underlying SMT and discusses its potential as a scalable strategy for managing hrHPV-associated disease within existing cervical cancer prevention frameworks.

We outline the ecological principles underpinning SMT and discuss its development as a potentially scalable microbiome-directed strategy for restoring cervicovaginal health and managing hrHPV-associated disease within existing cervical cancer prevention frameworks.

papers.title: [Update on immunotherapy in head and neck cancer : New aspects from the ASCO annual meeting 2026].
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) targeting PD-1/PD-L1 have reshaped the treatment of head and neck squamous cell carcinoma, but durable benefit remains limited to selected subgroups. New perioperative and palliative strategies, including bispecific and T‐cell receptor (TCR)-based approaches, aim to overcome immunosuppressive barriers and improve long-term control. OBJECTIVE: Immunotherapy trials in head and neck cancer presented at the 2026 American Society of Clinical Oncology (ASCO) Annual Meeting were systematically reviewed and their impact on current standards and future strategies in frontline and recurrent/metastatic settings was analyzed. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Clinical trials of PD-1/PD-L1-based therapies, bispecific antibodies, and innovative strategies in curative and palliative head and neck cancer were reviewed, based on abstracts and presentations at ASCO 2026. RESULTS: In the curative setting, a perioperative and adjuvant PD-1-based strategy with pembrolizumab provided consistent survival benefits and reduced pathological high-risk features while preserving surgical radicality. Neoadjuvant bispecific PD-1/vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) blockade combined with chemotherapy achieved high response rates and organ-preserving resections, whereas adjuvant CD40-targeted vaccination in human papillomavirus (HPV)16-positive oropharyngeal head and neck squamous cell carcinoma induced robust, durable T‐cell responses. In the recurrent/metastatic setting, PD-1-based combinations with targeted agents improved tumor response, disease control, and survival. Bispecific epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)-directed antibodies and the TCR-based bispecific T‐cell engaging receptor (TCER) IMA401 showed meaningful activity after PD‐1 failure. CONCLUSION: These data support the expansion of immuno-oncologic concepts into perioperative and palliative settings. Bispecific and TCR-based strategies signal a shift from conventional ICI monotherapy toward more differentiated, mechanism-driven combination approaches.

analysis.summary_en: This review focuses on the role of human papillomaviruses (HPV) in head and neck cancer, particularly in the context of immunotherapy. It highlights the limited durable benefit of PD-1/PD-L1-based immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma, with consistent survival advantages observed in perioperative and adjuvant settings using pembrolizumab. The review also discusses the potential of bispecific antibodies and TCR-based strategies, such as IMA401, to improve outcomes after PD-1 failure. In the recurrent/metastatic setting, PD-1-based combinations with targeted agents showed improved tumor response, disease control, and survival. The findings suggest a shift from conventional ICI monotherapy to more tailored, mechanism-driven approaches in HPV-associated head and neck cancers. The review is based on abstracts and presentations from the 2026 American Society of Clinical Oncology (ASCO) Annual Meeting, emphasizing the need for further research and application of these strategies in clinical practice.

papers.abstract_zh: 背景:针对 PD-1/PD-L1 的免疫检查点抑制剂 (ICIs) 重塑了头颈鳞状细胞癌的 治疗,但持久益处仍然仅限于选定的亚组。新的围手术期和姑息治疗策略,包括双特异性和基于 T 细胞受体 (TCR) 的方法,旨在克服免疫抑制障碍并改善长期控制。目的:系统回顾了 2026 年美国临床肿瘤学会 (ASCO) 年会上提出的头颈癌免疫治疗试验,并分析了它们对一线和复发/转移环境中当前标准和未来策略的影响。材料和方法:根据 ASCO 2026 上的摘要和演讲,对基于 PD-1/PD-L1 的疗法、双特异性抗体以及头颈癌治疗和姑息性创新策略的临床试验进行了回顾。结果:在治疗环境中,基于帕博利珠单抗的围手术期和辅助 PD-1 策略提供了一致的生存获益,并减少了病理高风险特征,同时保留了手术根治性。新辅助双特异性 PD-1/血管内皮生长因子 (VEGF) 阻断联合化疗实现了高缓解率和器官保留切除,而辅助 CD40 靶向 疫苗接种 在 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV)16 阳性口咽头颈鳞状细胞癌中诱导了强大、持久的 T 细胞反应。在复发/转移性疾病中,基于 PD-1 的靶向药物组合可改善肿瘤反应、疾病控制和生存。双特异性表皮生长因子受体 (EGFR) 导向抗体和基于 TCR 的双特异性 T 细胞接合受体 (TCER) IMA401 在 PD-1 失败后显示出有意义的活性。结论:这些数据支持将免疫肿瘤学概念扩展到围手术期和姑息治疗环境中。双特异性和基于 TCR 的策略标志着从传统 ICI 单一疗法向更加差异化、机制驱动的联合疗法的转变。

papers.title: HPV-associated extracellular vesicles and the tumor microenvironment: mechanisms of immune modulation and translational implications
papers.abstract: Human papillomavirus infections are a major cause of cervical cancer and are also associated with several anogenital and oropharyngeal malignancies. Persistent infection with high-risk HPV types and sustained expression of viral oncoproteins E6 and E7 contribute to malignant transformation. Extracellular vesicles are increasingly recognized as important mediators of intercellular communication and can transfer proteins, nucleic acids, lipids, and other regulatory molecules between cells. HPV-associated changes in EV cargo, such as viral transcripts, may influence immune and stromal cells within the tumor microenvironment. Experimental studies have implicated HPV-associated EVs in the regulation of dendritic cell function, macrophage polarization, T-cell responses, immune checkpoint signaling, chronic inflammation, and mechanisms related to viral persistence and immune evasion. Cell-based and preclinical studies also suggest that EVs released by HPV-positive tumor cells may contribute to related disorders including angiogenesis and metastatic progression. On the other hand, human studies have primarily provided observational evidence linking EV-associated molecular profiles with HPV status or disease characteristics. Beyond these mechanistic insights, a growing body of work explores the translational potential of EVs, including their use as liquid-biopsy biomarkers and as engineered delivery platforms such as Nefmut-based vesicles carrying HPV16 E7 that elicit protective CD8 + T-cell responses in preclinical models. This narrative review, with emphasis on tumor-immune interactions, and also discusses emerging diagnostic and therapeutic applications together with the methodological and clinical barriers that must be addressed before EV-based strategies can be translated into routine practice.

analysis.summary_en: This review focuses on the role of human papillomaviruses (HPV) in the tumor microenvironment, particularly their association with cervical cancer and other malignancies. It highlights the mechanisms by which HPV-associated extracellular vesicles (EVs) modulate immune responses, including effects on dendritic cells, macrophages, and T-cell activity. The review also discusses the potential of EVs as biomarkers and therapeutic tools, such as engineered Nefmut-based vesicles carrying HPV16 E7. However, it notes that human studies have mainly provided observational evidence, and there are gaps in understanding the full impact of EVs on disease progression and immune evasion. The review emphasizes the need to address methodological and clinical challenges before EV-based strategies can be applied in routine practice.

papers.title: Mechanisms of cetuximab resistance in head and neck squamous cell Carcinoma: Focus on the EGFR-ERK pathway.
papers.abstract: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) is the sixth most common cancer worldwide. Major risk factors include tobacco use, excessive alcohol consumption, and infection with oncogenic human papillomaviruses (HPV). Despite advances in treatment, HNSCC remains associated with poor outcomes, particularly in patients with advanced or recurrent/metastatic disease. The epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) has been recognized as a key oncogenic driver in HNSCC, as it is frequently overexpressed and promotes activation of multiple pro-tumorigenic signaling pathways, including ERK and PI3K/Akt. Cetuximab remains the only approved molecularly targeted agent directed against a tumor-associated receptor in HNSCC. However, its clinical benefit is limited by low response rates and the frequent development of resistance even in initially responsive tumors. Understanding the molecular basis of resistance to EGFR-targeted therapy is therefore critical for developing more effective pharmacological strategies and improving the clinical utility of cetuximab. In this review, we summarize EGFR alterations, activation of parallel compensatory pathways, and the reactivation of downstream signaling cascades, including PI3K/Akt and Ras/ERK, as major mechanisms underlying resistance to EGFR-targeted therapy in HNSCC. We focus particularly on the ERK signaling pathway as a central integrator of genetic, epigenetic, and adaptive resistance mechanisms. Sustained ERK activity restores downstream EGFR outputs, promotes feedback ligand production, drives epithelial-mesenchymal transition and cellular plasticity, and engages parallel oncogenic pathways, thereby enabling tumor cells to evade cetuximab-mediated EGFR blockade. Combined targeting of ERK and EGFR may therefore represent a promising strategy for overcoming cetuximab resistance in selected molecular contexts.

papers.title: POST-TREATMENT SURVEILLANCE AND MANAGEMENT OF RECURRENT CERVICAL CANCER - A REVIEW FROM THE FRENCH CERVICAL CANCER GUIDELINES GROUP.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To review the available evidence on post-treatment follow-up and recurrence management after cervical cancer. METHODS: We conducted a narrative review of the literature on surveillance modalities, and the management of pelvic and nodal recurrences. RESULTS: Most recurrences occur within three years of treatment, but the survival benefit of detection before symptom onset remains unproven. After fertility-sparing surgery, HPV testing is sensitive for detecting asymptomatic pelvic recurrence. After hysterectomy, most recurrences are symptomatic, and clinical examination has a higher diagnostic yield than HPV testing or vaginal vault cytology. After concurrent chemoradiotherapy (CRT), persistent HPV infection is associated with an increased recurrence risk, but its limited specificity and the absence of a validated HPV-based surveillance strategy restrict its clinical utility. MRI and FDG PET/CT are useful for response assessment and investigation of suspected recurrence, but evidence supporting routine imaging of asymptomatic patients is lacking. Intensive follow-up schedules have not improved recurrence detection or survival. Evidence on recurrence management is predominantly retrospective. Pelvic recurrences after primary surgery have been treated with CRT, supplemented by brachytherapy for vaginal involvement. In selected patients with central pelvic recurrence after CRT, complete surgical resection may provide prolonged survival, but carries substantial morbidity. Nodal recurrences outside previously irradiated fields have been treated with CRT. CONCLUSION: Available evidence supports a predominantly clinical, treatment-adapted follow-up. The survival benefit of intensive surveillance, routine imaging, or detecting asymptomatic recurrence remains uncertain. Recurrence management requires individualized multidisciplinary assessment based on disease extent, disease-free interval, and previous treatments.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review aims to evaluate post-treatment follow-up and recurrence management strategies for cervical cancer, focusing on the role of human papillomaviruses (HPV) in recurrence detection and treatment.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a narrative synthesis of the literature on surveillance methods and recurrence management, with an emphasis on HPV testing and imaging techniques. It includes evidence on the timing of recurrences, the utility of HPV testing in different treatment contexts, and the role of imaging modalities.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The evidence suggests that most cervical cancer recurrences occur within three years of treatment, but the survival benefit of early detection remains unproven. Clinical examination is more effective than HPV testing or vaginal vault cytology in detecting recurrences after hysterectomy, while HPV testing is sensitive for asymptomatic pelvic recurrence following fertility-sparing surgery. Persistent HPV infection is linked to increased recurrence risk after CRT, but its clinical utility is limited due to low specificity and lack of a validated strategy.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: There is uncertainty regarding the survival benefit of intensive surveillance or routine imaging in asymptomatic patients. The evidence is largely retrospective, and there is a lack of robust data supporting the routine use of imaging for asymptomatic individuals. Additionally, the role of HPV in recurrence management after CRT is not fully established due to limited specificity and absence of a validated strategy.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Further research is needed to determine the clinical utility of HPV-based surveillance strategies and to validate the effectiveness of imaging modalities in asymptomatic patients. Practice should focus on individualized, multidisciplinary approaches for recurrence management, considering disease extent, disease-free interval, and prior treatments.

analysis.summary_en: This review evaluates post-treatment surveillance and management of recurrent cervical cancer, emphasizing the role of human papillomaviruses (HPV) in recurrence detection. It highlights that most recurrences occur within three years of treatment, but the survival benefit of early detection remains unproven. HPV testing is effective for asymptomatic pelvic recurrence after fertility-sparing surgery, while clinical examination is more sensitive for detecting recurrences after hysterectomy. Persistent HPV infection is associated with higher recurrence risk after concurrent chemoradiotherapy (CRT), but its clinical utility is limited due to low specificity and lack of a validated strategy. The review underscores the need for individualized, multidisciplinary approaches in managing recurrences and calls for further research to clarify the role of HPV-based surveillance and imaging in asymptomatic patients.

papers.abstract_zh: 目的:回顾 治疗 后随访和 宫颈癌 后复发管理的现有证据。方法:我们对 监测 模式以及盆腔和淋巴结复发治疗的文献进行了叙述性回顾。结果:大多数复发发生在 治疗 治疗后三年内,但症状出现前检测的生存益处尚未得到证实。保留生育能力手术后,HPV 检测对于检测无症状盆腔复发非常敏感。子宫切除术后,大多数复发都是有症状的,临床检查比 HPV 检测或阴道穹窿细胞学检查具有更高的诊断率。同步放化疗(CRT)后,持续性 HPV 感染与复发风险增加相关,但其特异性有限且缺乏基于 HPV 的经过验证的 监测 策略限制了其临床应用。MRI 和 FDG PET/CT 可用于疗效评估和疑似复发调查,但缺乏支持无症状患者常规影像学检查的证据。密集的随访计划并没有改善复发检测或生存率。关于复发管理的证据主要是回顾性的。初次手术后盆腔复发可采用 CRT 治疗,并辅以近距离放射治疗治疗阴道受累。在 CRT 后出现中央盆腔复发的特定患者中,完全手术切除可能会延长生存期,但会带来较高的发病率。先前照射区域外的淋巴结复发已采用 CRT 进行治疗。结论:现有证据支持主要临床、治疗 适应的随访。强化 监测、常规成像或检测无症状复发的生存获益仍不确定。复发管理需要根据疾病程度、无病间隔和既往 治疗 进行个体化多学科评估。

analysis_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述旨在评估治疗后的随访和复发管理策略,重点关注人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)在复发检测和治疗中的作用。
analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述是对 监测 方法和复发管理文献的叙述性综合,重点是 HPV 检测和成像技术。它包括有关复发时间、HPV 检测在不同 治疗 背景下的效用以及成像方式的作用的证据。
analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 证据表明,大多数 宫颈癌 复发发生在 治疗 的三年内,但早期检测的生存益处尚未得到证实。在检测子宫切除术后的复发方面,临床检查比 HPV 检测或阴道穹窿细胞学检查更有效,而 HPV 检测对保留生育手术后的无症状盆腔复发敏感。持续的 HPV 感染与 CRT 后复发风险增加有关,但由于特异性低且缺乏经过验证的策略,其临床实用性受到限制。
analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 对于无症状患者,强化 监测 或常规影像学检查的生存获益尚不确定。证据主要是回顾性的,缺乏可靠的数据支持对无症状个体进行常规影像学检查。此外,由于特异性有限且缺乏经过验证的策略,HPV 在 CRT 后复发管理中的作用尚未完全确定。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 需要进一步的研究来确定基于 HPV 的 监测 策略的临床效用,并验证成像方式对无症状患者的有效性。实践应侧重于复发管理的个体化、多学科方法,考虑疾病范围、无病间隔和既往 治疗。

papers.title: Advanced Anal Squamous Cell Carcinoma in the Chemoimmunotherapy Era: Retifanlimab, Nivolumab, and a Practical Framework for Treatment Selection.
papers.abstract: Advanced anal squamous cell carcinoma (ASCC) is a rare human papillomavirus-associated malignancy with historically limited prospective evidence for systemic therapy. InterAAct established carboplatin-paclitaxel as a clinically favorable chemotherapy backbone compared with cisplatin-fluorouracil. POD1UM-303/InterAACT-2 subsequently showed that adding retifanlimab significantly improved progression-free survival in patients with no prior systemic therapy for advanced disease. At the final overall-survival analysis, median overall survival was 32.8 versus 22.2 months (HR 0.75, 95% CI 0.55-1.01); the regimen has received regulatory authorization in the United States, the European Union, and Japan. EA2176 is evaluating carboplatin-paclitaxel with or without nivolumab and will clarify whether first-line PD-1-based chemoimmunotherapy represents a reproducible class effect. This focused narrative review critically summarizes the evidence for retifanlimab- and nivolumab-based strategies and proposes a practical framework for treatment selection. Key considerations include performance status, immune-checkpoint-inhibitor eligibility, HIV infection, autoimmune risk, neuropathy, organ function, tumor burden, local symptom control, and post-chemoimmunotherapy sequencing. Retifanlimab plus carboplatin-paclitaxel currently has the most mature phase III evidence, whereas nivolumab-based chemoimmunotherapy remains investigational pending EA2176. Treatment decisions should distinguish phase III-validated options from class-effect extrapolation and integrate multidisciplinary local therapy when appropriate.

papers.title: From HPV Genetic Diversity to Precision Therapeutics: Viral-Host Interactions and Emerging Strategies for Cervical Cancer Prevention and Treatment
papers.abstract: Cervical cancer is a major global health challenge, especially in low- and middle-income countries, despite the availability of effective prophylactic human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccines, screening methods and established treatments. Cervical cancer is primarily caused by persistent infection with high-risk HPV, but persistent infection is necessary, but not sufficient, for the development of cancer. Advances in understanding HPV genetic diversity, viral persistence, and virus-host molecular interactions are creating new opportunities to improve precision in HPV prevention and treatment. HPV genotype distribution and differences in oncogenic potential inform vaccine development and screening strategies. The viral oncoproteins E6 and E7 disrupt host tumor-suppressor pathways, driving cellular immortalization and genomic instability. Molecular events such as viral insertion, epigenetic modifications, APOBEC-associated mutations, and immune escape contribute to disease progression. These discoveries have revealed molecular vulnerabilities that can be targeted therapeutically. Immune checkpoint inhibitors and antibody-drug conjugates are used clinically in specific contexts of cervical cancer presentation and treatment. At the same time, therapeutic vaccines, adoptive cellular immunotherapies, RNA interference, and genome editing are being investigated as complementary strategies to target HPV-associated cervical cancer. With advances in next-generation sequencing, molecular biomarkers, and artificial intelligence, these tools could further refine risk stratification and therapy selection. This review explores the current understanding of HPV genetic variation and virus-host interactions driving a shift from traditional prevention and treatment strategies to precision prevention and targeted therapeutics, and critically assesses remaining challenges.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Cervical cancer remains a major global health challenge, especially in low- and middle-income countries, despite the availability of effective prophylactic human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccines, screening methods and established treatments. The study aims to explore the current understanding of HPV genetic variation and virus-host interactions driving a shift from traditional prevention and treatment strategies to precision prevention and targeted therapeutics.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study is a review of current literature on HPV genetic diversity, viral persistence, and virus-host molecular interactions. It focuses on HPV-associated cervical cancer and other explicitly HPV-related diseases, including cervical intraepithelial neoplasia, HPV-associated anal cancer, and HPV-associated oropharyngeal cancer.
analysis.methods: The study utilizes next-generation sequencing, molecular biomarkers, and artificial intelligence to refine risk stratification and therapy selection for HPV-associated diseases.
analysis.main_results: The study reports that HPV genotype distribution and differences in oncogenic potential inform vaccine development and screening strategies. It also highlights that molecular events such as viral insertion, epigenetic modifications, APOBEC-associated mutations, and immune escape contribute to disease progression.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that the discoveries reveal molecular vulnerabilities that can be targeted therapeutically. This represents a novel approach to cervical cancer prevention and treatment by leveraging HPV genetic diversity and virus-host interactions.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform the development of more precise prevention and treatment strategies for HPV-associated cervical cancer, potentially improving outcomes in affected populations.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is a review and does not present original data, thus the evidence strength is moderate. The limitations include the reliance on existing literature and the absence of new experimental results.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the role of human papillomavirus (HPV) genetic diversity and virus-host interactions in cervical cancer prevention and treatment. It highlights the importance of HPV genotype distribution and oncogenic potential in shaping vaccine development and screening strategies. The study also discusses molecular mechanisms such as viral insertion, epigenetic modifications, APOBEC-associated mutations, and immune escape that contribute to disease progression. The authors emphasize the potential of targeting molecular vulnerabilities for therapeutic interventions. While the study provides valuable insights into the shift from traditional to precision approaches, it is limited by its reliance on existing literature and the absence of new experimental data. The findings have significant implications for improving surveillance, diagnosis, and treatment of HPV-associated cervical cancer, particularly in low- and middle-income countries.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 尽管有有效的预防药物 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 疫苗、筛查方法和已建立的 治疗,宫颈癌 仍然是一个重大的全球健康挑战,特别是在低收入和中等收入国家。该研究旨在探讨目前对HPV遗传变异和病毒-宿主相互作用的理解,推动从传统预防和治疗策略向精准预防和靶向治疗的转变。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究回顾了有关 HPV 遗传多样性、病毒持久性和病毒-宿主 分子相互作用的最新文献。它重点关注 HPV 相关的 宫颈癌 和其他明确与 HPV 相关的疾病,包括宫颈上皮内瘤变、HPV 相关的肛门癌和 HPV 相关的口咽癌。
elements_zh.methods: 该研究利用下一代测序、分子生物标志物和人工智能来完善 HPV 相关疾病的风险分层和治疗选择。
elements_zh.main_results: 该研究报告称,HPV 基因型分布和致癌潜力的差异为 疫苗 的开发和筛查策略提供了信息。它还强调了病毒插入、表观遗传修饰、APOBEC 相关 突变 和免疫逃逸等分子事件有助于疾病进展。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,这些发现揭示了可以作为治疗目标的分子漏洞。这代表了一种利用 HPV 遗传多样性和病毒-宿主 相互作用来预防 宫颈癌 和 治疗 的新方法。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为针对 HPV 相关 宫颈癌 制定更精确的预防和 治疗 策略提供信息,从而有可能改善受影响人群的结果。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究为综述,不提供原始数据,因此证据强度中等。局限性包括依赖现有文献和缺乏新的实验结果。

papers.abstract_zh: 尽管有有效的预防药物 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 疫苗、筛查方法和已建立的 治疗,宫颈癌 仍然是一项重大的全球健康挑战,特别是在低收入和中等收入国家。宫颈癌主要是由高危型HPV持续感染引起的,但持续感染对于癌症的发展是必要的,但还不够充分。在了解 HPV 遗传多样性、病毒持久性和病毒-宿主 分子相互作用方面取得的进展,为提高 HPV 预防和 治疗 的精确度创造了新的机会。HPV 基因型分布和致癌潜力的差异为 疫苗 的开发和筛查策略提供信息。病毒癌蛋白 E6 和 E7 破坏 宿主 肿瘤抑制途径,驱动细胞永生化和基因组不稳定。病毒插入、表观遗传修饰、APOBEC 相关 突变 和免疫逃逸等分子事件有助于疾病进展。这些发现揭示了可以作为治疗目标的分子漏洞。免疫检查点抑制剂和抗体药物偶联物在 宫颈癌 呈现和 治疗 的特定背景下临床使用。与此同时,正在研究治疗性 疫苗、过继性细胞免疫疗法、RNA 干扰和 基因组 编辑,作为针对 HPV 相关 宫颈癌 的补充策略。随着下一代测序、分子生物标志物和人工智能的进步,这些工具可以进一步完善风险分层和治疗选择。本综述探讨了目前对 HPV 遗传变异和病毒与 宿主 相互作用的理解,推动了从传统预防和 治疗 策略向精准预防和靶向治疗的转变,并严格评估了剩余的挑战。

papers.title: [Radiotherapy of head and neck cancer : Highlights from the 2026 ASCO Annual Meeting].
papers.abstract: At the 2026 American Society of Clinical Oncology (ASCO) Annual Meeting, several studies focused on radiotherapy of head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC). The phase III AREST trial showed that adjuvant radiotherapy for early oral cavity cancer with intermediate-risk features can reduce the risk of locoregional recurrence. A post hoc analysis of the JCOG1008 trial found no increased locoregional recurrence rate even when adjuvant chemoradiotherapy was initiated later than recommended. Combined radioimmunotherapy (RIT) was also a major topic this year: in a subgroup analysis of the NIVOPOSTOP trial, the disease-free survival (DFS) benefit of nivolumab was maintained in patients with extensive neck dissection, which weakens the frequently highlighted mechanistic relevance of regional lymph nodes for the immune response. In the treatment of human papillomavirus (HPV)-positive oropharyngeal cancer, results for RIT were conflicting: the phase II CCTG HN.9 trial evaluating radiotherapy combined with durvalumab failed to meet its efficacy endpoint, whereas the phase II KEYCHAIN trial of definitive RIT with pembrolizumab demonstrated a significant improvement in progression-free survival (PFS) compared with cisplatin-based chemoradiotherapy. In addition, a subgroup analysis of the combined positive score (CPS) ≥ 10 population of the KEYNOTE-412 trial underscored the importance of biomarker-based patient selection when combining radiotherapy and immunotherapy.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on the role of human papillomaviruses (HPV) in the context of head and neck cancer, particularly in relation to radiotherapy and its impact on locoregional recurrence and survival outcomes. The central question is whether HPV-associated diseases, such as oropharyngeal cancer, benefit from specific radiotherapy approaches, including combined radioimmunotherapy.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is based on findings from the 2026 ASCO Annual Meeting, including the phase III AREST trial, the post hoc analysis of the JCOG1008 trial, and subgroup analyses from the NIVOPOSTOP and KEYNOTE-412 trials. These studies were selected based on their relevance to HPV-associated diseases and their focus on radiotherapy outcomes. The review does not explicitly describe a meta-analysis or consensus process, but it summarizes key results from these trials.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review highlights that adjuvant radiotherapy for early oral cavity cancer with intermediate-risk features can reduce locoregional recurrence. Additionally, it notes that the DFS benefit of nivolumab in combined radioimmunotherapy (RIT) is maintained in patients with extensive neck dissection, suggesting that regional lymph nodes may not be as critical for immune response as previously thought. However, the results for RIT in HPV-positive oropharyngeal cancer are conflicting, with the CCTG HN.9 trial failing to meet its efficacy endpoint and the KEYCHAIN trial showing significant improvement in progression-free survival (PFS) compared with cisplatin-based chemoradiotherapy.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: There is controversy regarding the efficacy of combined radioimmunotherapy (RIT) in HPV-positive oropharyngeal cancer, as the CCTG HN.9 trial did not meet its efficacy endpoint while the KEYCHAIN trial showed significant improvement in PFS. Additionally, the review notes that subgroup analyses of the KEYNOTE-412 trial emphasize the importance of biomarker-based patient selection when combining radiotherapy and immunotherapy, indicating a gap in understanding how to optimally select patients for such treatments.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review suggests that future research should focus on refining biomarker-based patient selection for combined radiotherapy and immunotherapy approaches in HPV-associated cancers. It also highlights the need for further studies to resolve the conflicting results on the efficacy of RIT in HPV-positive oropharyngeal cancer. In practice, these findings may inform treatment strategies for patients with HPV-associated head and neck cancers, particularly those with intermediate-risk features or extensive neck dissection.

analysis.summary_en: This review summarizes key findings from the 2026 ASCO Annual Meeting on the role of human papillomaviruses (HPV) in head and neck cancer, particularly in relation to radiotherapy. It highlights that adjuvant radiotherapy can reduce locoregional recurrence in early oral cavity cancer with intermediate-risk features. However, results for combined radioimmunotherapy (RIT) in HPV-positive oropharyngeal cancer are conflicting, with some trials showing no benefit and others demonstrating improved progression-free survival. The review also emphasizes the importance of biomarker-based patient selection in these treatment approaches. These findings suggest the need for further research to clarify the efficacy of RIT and to optimize patient selection for combined therapies.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述重点关注 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 在头颈癌中的作用,特别是与放射治疗及其对局部复发和生存结果的影响有关。核心问题是口咽癌等 HPV 相关疾病是否受益于特定的放射治疗方法,包括联合放射免疫治疗。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该审查基于 2026 年 ASCO 年会的结果,包括 III 期 AREST 试验、JCOG1008 试验的事后分析以及 NIVOPOSTOP 和 KEYNOTE-412 试验的亚组分析。这些研究的选择是基于它们与 HPV 相关疾病的相关性以及它们对放射治疗结果的关注。该综述没有明确描述荟萃分析或共识过程,但总结了这些试验的主要结果。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 该综述强调,对具有中等风险特征的早期口腔癌进行辅助放疗可以减少局部复发。此外,它指出,纳武单抗在联合放射​​免疫治疗 (RIT) 中的 DFS 益处在广泛颈清扫患者中得以维持,这表明区域淋巴结对于 免疫应答 可能并不像之前认为的那么重要。然而,RIT 在 HPV 阳性口咽癌中的结果是相互矛盾的,CCTG HN.9 试验未能达到其疗效终点,而 KEYCHAIN 试验显示与基于顺铂的放化疗相比,无进展生存期 (PFS) 显着改善。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 关于联合放射免疫治疗 (RIT) 对 HPV 阳性口咽癌的疗效存在争议,因为 CCTG HN.9 试验未达到其疗效终点,而 KEYCHAIN 试验显示 PFS 显着改善。此外,该评论指出,KEYNOTE-412 试验的亚组分析强调了在放射治疗和免疫治疗相结合时基于生物标志物的患者选择的重要性,这表明在理解如何为此类 治疗 最佳选择患者方面存在差距。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 该综述表明,未来的研究应重点关注针对 HPV 相关癌症的联合放疗和免疫治疗方法,完善基于生物标志物的患者选择。它还强调需要进一步研究来解决 RIT 对 HPV 阳性口咽癌疗效的相互矛盾的结果。在实践中,这些发现可能为 HPV 相关头颈癌患者的 治疗 策略提供参考,特别是那些具有中等风险特征或广泛颈清扫术的患者。
