About Futurity Universities Science Health Culture Environment Videos Interviews Slideshows Audio Science Health Culture Environment Research news from top universities Subscribe 1793372627 New clue hints at how head and neck cancers spread October 30th, 2026 Posted by Washington U. in St. Louis (Credit: Getty Images) Share this Article Facebook Twitter Reddit Email You are free to share this article under the Attribution 4.0 International license. Tags cancer University Washington University in St. Louis Researchers have found that aggressive cancer cells can appear in different locations within head and neck tumors, providing new clues as to why some such cancers—particularly squamous cell carcinomas not caused by the human papillomavirus (HPV)—are more difficult to treat. In research in Nature Genetics, the researchers found two distinct spatial patterns, or locations, where aggressive cancer cells can occur. One location, which was previously known, is at the outer edge of a tumor as cells begin to invade surrounding tissue. The newly discovered location is within the core of some tumors. “Understanding the complex tumor ecosystem with spatial approaches is emerging as a critical tool to study cancer more broadly,” says Sidharth Puram, a professor and head of WashU Medicine’s otolaryngology—head and neck surgery department and senior author of the study. “By using these techniques, we can understand the components of the tumor, but also where those cells are from. In this case, we were quite surprised to see these aggressive cancer cells, which we call partial epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition, or EMT, in different locations. It completely upended our views on head and neck tumors.” Head and neck cancers are the sixth most common cancer worldwide, and there is increasing evidence that HPV is strongly associated with a subset of these cancers—particularly oropharyngeal cancers, which include cancers of the tonsils and the surrounding area in the middle part of the throat. The team of researchers studied tumors from patients diagnosed with HPV-positive, as well as HPV-negative, head and neck squamous cell carcinoma. By closing mapping where different cells reside within the tumors, the researchers discovered aggressive cancer cells deep inside the tumors of some patients. Further study found that these deeper cancer cells appeared to take on a more aggressive state after interacting with certain immune cells, in response to signals involving a protein called Oncostatin M (OSM). Puram explains that when these aggressive cells were at the edge of a tumor, they were activated by signals from fibroblast cells, which are part of a tumor’s structural elements. However, in the core these aggressive cells were typically found in proximity to concentrations of immune-response macrophage cells that normally digest cellular waste products and foreign substances. These macrophages release the activating OSM signal. “This distinction is critical, as we must target these triggers differently in edge versus core tumors,” he says. “Fortunately, in each case, there are therapeutic agents that are being developed.” While most of the aggressive cells were present at the edge, up to one-third had the more distinct core pattern of distribution in HPV-negative cancers. Notably, Puram says, “We are trying to understand how these different locations affect tumor response to treatment and patient outcomes.” If researchers can figure out how to block the signal or signals that make these cancer cells more aggressive, it could lead to potential new treatment strategies for head and neck cancers. Right now, the research is in its early stages. “It’s a clue,” Puram stresses. “We have an important clue that increases our understanding of how head and neck cancers potentially behave and spread. But it’s significant because it may lead to the development of more effective options to treat some of the most difficult forms of this type of cancer.” Source: Washington University in St. Louis Related Cancer deaths tied to alcohol doubled between 1990 and 2023 ‘Dialogue’ with environment fuels cancer stem cells Head and neck cancers hijack nearby healthy tissue Stay Connected. Show results from: Clear search input Search for result Max Clear search input Search for result Press release “MY CHOICE – A FUTURE PROTECTED FROM CANCER”: Young people turn HPV awareness into peer-to-peer learning 29 October 2026 UNICEF/2026/Moldova/DanBragoi Română English русский Chișinău, 27 October 2026 – Adolescents across all districts of the Republic of Moldova will learn about human papillomavirus (HPV) prevention and the importance of vaccination through the “My Choice – A Future Protected from Cancer” awareness and behaviour change campaign, which aims to build confidence in HPV vaccination. Through interactive games, presentations and peer-to-peer discussions, Youth Klinic Moldova volunteers will share reliable, medically accurate information with their peers, helping them distinguish myths from evidence-based facts. The campaign aims to raise awareness among adolescents about the role of HPV vaccination in preventing HPV-related cancers and to improve access to accurate, evidence-based information for young people and parents. To achieve this, the campaign will mobilize the Youth Klinic Moldova volunteer network, active across 40 youth-friendly health centres, to conduct peer-to-peer awareness activities in schools and communities, including activities involving refugee adolescents. The campaign will also engage young people online through reels, videos, articles and content co-created with adolescents. By using engaging, youth-friendly digital content, including materials developed by young people themselves, the campaign will address common myths, encourage informed decision-making and promote open dialogue and youth participation. Young people and parents who have questions about HPV and vaccination are encouraged to consult their family doctor or visit their nearest Youth Klinic Moldova centre. For information and guidance, they can contact the YOUTH KLINIC SUPPORT LINE at 0 800 800 22. Young people can also submit questions through YKChat, an online counselling service available on Telegram. HPV vaccination is available free of charge in the Republic of Moldova for girls and boys aged 9–26. For children aged 9–14, the vaccination schedule consists of a single dose, while adolescents and young adults aged 15–26 receive two doses administered six months apart. HPV vaccination coverage in the Republic of Moldova remains low. According to the latest available data, just over 46% of girls aged 10–14 have been vaccinated against HPV, compared with approximately 4% of boys in the same age group. Increasing vaccination coverage, alongside screening and timely treatment, is essential to achieving the goal of eliminating cervical cancer as a public health problem. The “My Choice – A Future Protected from Cancer” awareness and behaviour change campaign, aimed at increasing confidence in and demand for HPV vaccination, is implemented by UNICEF, the NGO Health for Youth, and the network of Youth-Friendly Health Centres – Youth Klinic Moldova, in partnership with the Ministry of Health and the Ministry of Education and Research, with financial support from the German Government through the German Development Bank (KfW) and the UK Government. Media contacts Valeria Dumitriu Communication Officer UNICEF Moldova Email: vdumitriu@unicef.org About UNICEF UNICEF promotes the rights and wellbeing of every child, in everything we do. Together with our partners, we work in 190 countries and territories to translate that commitment into practical action, focusing special effort on reaching the most vulnerable and excluded children, to the benefit of all children, everywhere. Send Close Online First Share on Facebook Share on LinkedIn Share on X Email Article Copy Article Url Print OCTOBER 30, 2026 More HPV Doses Are Associated With Lower Cervical Cancer Incidence Originally published by our sister publication Specialty Pharmacy Continuum By Marcus A. Banks Two or three HPV vaccine doses are associated with a lower incidence of cervical cancer than one dose, according to a retrospective analysis from the West Virginia University (WVU) School of Pharmacy. The analysis earned a platinum abstract award at AMCP Nexus 2026, in San Diego. manassanant - stock.adobe.com More than 60% of participants in the analysis had received Gardasil 9 (human papillomavirus 9-valent vaccine, recombinant, Merck). The authors are planning subgroup analyses of vaccine type in future work. The CDC recommends that people with robust immune systems receive two doses of the HPV vaccine if the first dose occurs before 15 years of age, or three doses if the first HPV vaccine occurs at 15 years or later. Anyone who is immunocompromised should also receive three HPV vaccine doses, per the CDC. “Not every HPV infection will lead to cervical cancer. Only persistent high-risk HPV infections can result in [the malignancy],” noted study author Saba Dangpiaei, PharmD, MBA, who is pursuing a doctorate in health services and outcomes research at WVU, in Morgantown. “Our results focus on incidence of cervical cancer, not of HPV infection.” Dr. Dangpiaei and her colleagues analyzed the TriNetX electronic health record, associating cervical cancer diagnoses with the numbers of HPV vaccine doses received. This data set is imperfect, Dr. Dangpiaei acknowledged; for instance, someone may appear as having received two doses but in fact they received a third dose that had not been recorded. For their analysis, the WVU researchers included 512 girls and women aged 9 to 45 years, respectively, who received one, two, or three doses of the HPV vaccine. They used propensity score matching to ensure the dose cohorts were comparable to each other in terms of comorbidities. Most patients were white and received their first dose between 18 and 29 years of age. Dr. Dangpiaei and colleagues found that two and three HPV vaccine doses were associated with a lower likelihood of cervical cancer than one dose (two-dose hazard ratio [HR], 0.68; 95% CI, 0.53-0.89; P=0.004 and three-dose HR, 0.54; 95% CI, 0.42-0.68; P<0.001). Every year of delay before receiving a first HPV vaccine dose was associated with higher cervical cancer risk: when one dose was compared with two doses (HR, 1.06; 95% CI, 1.04-1.07), one dose compared with three doses (HR, 1.06; 95% CI, 1.05-1.08), or two doses compared with three (HR, 1.08; 95% CI, 1.06-1.09; all P<0.001). Insurers should support patients receiving two or three HPV vaccine doses, Dr. Dangpiaei advised. “Receiving a higher number of doses of HPV vaccine was significantly associated with lower risk of cervical cancer,” she said. Dr. Dangpiaei emphasized that the results do not imply that receiving a lower number of vaccine doses causes a higher risk for cervical cancer. “In lower resource settings it’s good to receive even a single dose of HPV vaccine. One single dose is way better than no dose at all,” she said. In 2022, WHO announced that a single dose of HPV vaccination could provide comparable protection to two doses, in healthy girls and women aged 9 to 20 years. WHO aimed to simplify follow-up requirements for completing a full vaccine series, which can be expensive. Dr. Dangpiaei reported no relevant financial disclosures. 2026 Volume 32 Issue Spec 11 Pages: SP612 Never-Screened Cervical Cancer Rates Climb Among US Women Author(s)Giuliana Grossi Fact checked by: Nicole Canfora Lupo Nearly 1 in 3 women aged 21 to 29 years and 1 in 7 aged 30 to 65 years had never been screened for cervical cancer by 2023. Advertisement Nearly 1 in 3 women aged 21 to 29 years had never been screened for cervical cancer. Image credit: art4stock - stock.adobe.com Nearly 1 in 3 women aged 21 to 29 years had never been screened for cervical cancer by 2023, up from roughly 1 in 8 in 2005, according to a new research letter published in JAMA Network Open.1 The study found the share of never-screened women aged 30 to 65 years also grew over the same period, reaching approximately 1 in 7. Never-Screened Rates Nearly Tripled Among Younger Women Drawing on 9 cycles of the National Health Interview Survey (NHIS) conducted between 2005 and 2023, researchers found the proportion of women aged 21 to 29 years who reported never being screened for cervical cancer rose from 12.5% (3.5 million women) to 31.9% (6.2 million women), an average annual percentage change (AAPC) of 5.2% (95% CI, 4.3%-7.5%). The increase accelerated sharply after 2010, climbing at an annual rate of 7.9% (95% CI, 6.0%-14.4%) through 2023. Among women aged 30 to 65 years, never-screening rose from 5.3% (4.3 million) to 14.8% (9.2 million), an AAPC of 6.8% (95% CI, 3.1%-12.0%). Additionally, human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination uptake among women aged 21 to 29 years climbed from 5.7% in 2008 to 54.0% in 2019 but remains incomplete. The study authors noted that nearly 8 million women in this age group remain unvaccinated, and almost a third of them have also never been screened for cervical cancer. Sign in or sign up Advanced-Stage Diagnoses Are Also Increasing The researchers paired the survey findings with US Cancer Statistics incidence data from 2001 to 2023, stratified by age and stage at diagnosis. Among women aged 30 to 64 years, both regional-stage and distant-stage cervical cancer incidence increased by more than 2% annually after 2017. Among women 65 years and older, distant-stage incidence has been climbing since 2001. The authors cautioned that the study was not designed to establish a causal link between nonscreening and rising incidence, but rather to generate hypotheses for future research. An analysis of the 2023 NHIS cohort, comprising 8901 women aged 21 to 65 years, found substantial disparities. Among women aged 21 to 29 years, never-screening was highest among Asian women, at 44.3% (95% CI, 32.07%-56.58%), compared with 28.8% (95% CI, 25.07%-32.57%) among non-Hispanic White women. Educational attainment also tracked with screening gaps: 39.0% of women with only a high school diploma had never been screened, compared with 17.1% of those with a master’s or doctoral degree. Similar disparities by race and ethnicity, education, insurance status, and region emerged among women aged 30 to 65 years, with uninsured women and those living in the South facing elevated risk. Screening Guideline Confusion Compounds the Problem The findings track with a broader pattern of eroding cervical cancer prevention identified in other recent research.2 A December 2025 report on commercially insured US adults found that guideline-concordant cervical cancer screening adherence was below 10%, with rapid changes to US recommendations, including the 2012 addition of cotesting and the 2018 addition of primary HPV testing, contributing to confusion among patients and clinicians. That analysis similarly pointed to disparities by race and socioeconomic status as a persistent barrier to consistent screening. The authors of the new research letter called for targeted strategies to address structural barriers among racial and ethnic minority groups, uninsured women, and residents of Southern states, populations that face both lower screening rates and higher rates of late-stage diagnosis and mortality.1 Limitations of the study include its reliance on self-reported screening data, which is subject to recall bias, and the unavailability of HPV vaccination status in national cancer registries. Co-Diagnostics' Joint Venture CoSara Diagnostics Announces Publication of Peer-Reviewed HPV Screening Study Using CoSara's SARAGENE® Test PR Newswire Thu, October 29, 2026 at 8:00 AM CDT 7 min read CODX Follow-Up Biopsies Identified High-Grade Lesions or Cervical Cancer in 12 of 20 HPV-Positive Women, Including a Cohort with Predominantly Negative Cytology Results CoSara to Exhibit at MICROCON 2026, the Annual Congress of the Indian Association of Medical Microbiologists Co-Dx to Host HPV Screening Webinar on November 17 to Support Awareness Across South Asian Markets SALT LAKE CITY, Oct. 29, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Co-Diagnostics, Inc. (Nasdaq: CODX) ("Co-Dx" or "the Company"), a molecular diagnostics company with a unique, patented platform for the development of molecular diagnostic tests, today announced the publication of a peer-reviewed study using the SARAGENE® Human Papillomavirus High Risk (HPV-HR) Test manufactured by CoSara Diagnostics Pvt. Ltd. ("CoSara"), the Company's joint venture in India. The study, conducted by investigators at a local institution in Gujarat, India and published in Infectious Agents and Cancer, highlights the potential role of molecular HPV testing in identifying women who warrant further evaluation, even when cytology results are negative. Investigators used the SARAGENE® HPV-HR Test to screen samples from 625 women aged 30 to 60, collected through hospital and community screening settings in Central Gujarat, India. Twenty women tested positive for high-risk HPV; 18 had cytology results reported as negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy (NILM), while two had low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions (LSIL). Subsequent colposcopy and directed biopsy identified high-grade cervical lesions (CIN II/III) in nine women and invasive cervical carcinoma in three. The full article, "Cross-sectional assessment of high-risk HPV prevalence, genotype distribution, and associated socio-behavioural correlates among women in Central Gujarat, India," is available at https://doi.org/10.1186/s13027-026-00796-x. "Expanding access to molecular HPV testing is an important part of strengthening cervical cancer screening, particularly in regions where access to diagnostics remains limited," said Dwight Egan, Chief Executive Officer of Co-Diagnostics. "We are excited to see CoSara's SARAGENE® test used in published research that brings the importance of molecular screening into such clear focus. Our goal through CoSara is to make high-quality, affordable molecular diagnostics more accessible to laboratories and clinicians across India and South Asia." The SARAGENE® HPV-HR Test is a wet-reagent, laboratory-based multiplex real-time PCR assay that detects HPV-16, HPV-18 and a pooled group of 12 additional high-risk HPV genotypes. The test is authorized for testing in India and is not available for sale in the United States. The investigators noted that the findings are preliminary, given the study's design and the limited number of HPV-positive participants, and that larger studies are needed to confirm these findings. Story Continues The report comes as international efforts increasingly focus on expanding access to HPV-based cervical cancer screening. In July 2026, the World Health Organization issued guidance to help countries implement and scale HPV DNA-based screening programs. CoSara's manufacturing presence in India and regional distribution footprint provide a foundation for the Company's efforts to support broader access to molecular diagnostics. Earlier this year, Co-Dx announced the expansion of CoSara's commercial and distribution territory beyond India to include Bangladesh, Pakistan, Nepal and Sri Lanka, supporting commercialization of the SARAGENE® product line subject to applicable regulatory approvals. In January 2026, the Company reported that CoSara's network included more than 40 distributors across India. CoSara will exhibit at MICROCON 2026, the 49th Annual Congress of the Indian Association of Medical Microbiologists, taking place October 28 to November 1, 2026, at the All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS) Nagpur in Maharashtra, India. The five-day congress is expected to bring together hundreds of microbiologists and clinical researchers from across India, along with pathology laboratory leaders and diagnostics industry representatives. CoSara's booth will feature its molecular diagnostics portfolio, including the SARAGENE® product line. Co-Diagnostics is also developing a separate HPV test for the Co-Dx PCR Pro® platform*, extending its development efforts into near-patient molecular testing. The SARAGENE® wet-reagent assay used in this study is distinct from that development program; the study did not evaluate PCR Pro or its HPV test. In recognition of World Cervical Cancer Elimination Day, Co-Dx plans to host a webinar on HPV and cervical cancer screening on November 17, 2026, intended for healthcare providers, laboratory professionals and other stakeholders across South Asian markets. Interested parties may pre-register by emailing info@co-dx.com. *The Co-Dx PCR platform (including the PCR Home®, PCR Pro®, mobile app, and all associated tests) has not been cleared or authorized by the FDA, is subject to review by the FDA and/or other regulatory bodies and is not yet available for sale. About Co-Diagnostics, Inc.: Co-Diagnostics, Inc., a Utah corporation, is a molecular diagnostics company that develops, manufactures and markets state-of-the-art diagnostics technologies. The Company's technologies are utilized for tests that are designed using the detection and/or analysis of nucleic acid molecules (DNA or RNA). The Company also uses its proprietary technology to design specific tests for its Co-Dx PCR at-home and point-of-care platform (subject to regulatory review and not currently for sale) and to identify genetic markers for use in applications other than infectious disease. supplementary_news.content_title: Early ctDNA Clearance Linked to Improved Survival With Pembrolizumab Regimen in HPV-Negative HNSCC
supplementary_news.content: Clearance of circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) during treatment was associated with improved long-term overall survival (OS) among patients with human papillomavirus (HPV)–negative locally advanced head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) who received pembrolizumab (Keytruda) plus concurrent chemoradiotherapy, according to an exploratory ctDNA analysis of the phase 3 KEYNOTE-412 trial (NCT03040999) presented at the 2026 ESMO Congress.1 In the HPV-negative subgroup, ctDNA clearance at cycle 3, day 1 of treatment occurred in 76.8% of evaluable patients in the pembrolizumab arm (n = 155) vs 66.3% of those in the placebo arm (n = 166). Among patients who received pembrolizumab plus chemoradiotherapy, the 5-year OS rate was 72.9% for those who cleared ctDNA (n = 119) vs 38.9% for those who did not (n = 36; P < .001). Moreover, the 5-year event-free survival (EFS) rates with these respective groups were 63.1% vs 38.2%, respectively (P = .001). In the placebo arm 5-year EFS rates for patients who achieved ctDNA clearance (n = 110) vs those who did not (n = 56) was associated were 48.4% vs 35.5% (P = .011), respectively, with 5-year OS rates being 58.6% vs 48.2% (P = .075). In the pembrolizumab arm of the HPV-negative subgroup, the 5-year OS rate was 70.5% for patients with a maximum somatic allele frequency (MSAF) below the median (n = 106) compared with 55.8% for those with MSAF at or above the median (n = 95; P = .009). The 5-year EFS rates were 58.9% vs 51.2% (P = .086) each of the respective groups. Regarding the placebo arm, the 5-year EFS rates were 48.1% (n = 96) vs 38.1% (n = 108; P = .002) for patients below and above the MSAF median, respectively, and the 5-year OS rates were 58.3% vs 49.5% (P = .01). Overall, investigators noted baseline ctDNA levels as prognostic for both EFS and OS with pembrolizumab benefits seen across ctDNA levels in HPV-negative HNSCC. For those with ctDNA clearance at cycle 3, day 1 and HPV-negative HNSCC, the clearance was predictive for long-term survival with pembrolizumab plus chemoradiotherapy regardless of other common prognostic markers. "However, [these] results should be interpreted with caution as the HPV-positive group sample size was small,” said lead study author Jean-Pascal Machiels, MD, PhD, in a presentation of the data. Machiels is the head of Adult and Pediatric Oncology at Institut Roi Albert II, Cliniques universitaires Saint-Luc, UCLouvain in Brusselsm Belgium. How was the ctDNA analysis of the phase 3 KEYNOTE-412 trial designed? The trial enrolled patients with evaluable tumor burden per RECIST 1.1 criteria and an ECOG performance status of 0 or 1, in addition to those who had not received prior surgical debulking for the head and neck.2 If patients received prior anti–PD-1, anti–PD-L1, anti–PD-L2 therapy, received a live vaccine within 30 days of their first dose, had active hepatitis B or C or had cancer outside oropharynx, larynx or oral cavity they were not enrolled in the trial. KEYNOTE-412 randomly assigned 804 patients with unresected, high-risk locally advanced HNSCC to pembrolizumab or placebo plus chemotherapy. Patients received pembrolizumab at 200 mg intravenously every 3 weeks for 3 doses with 6 to 7 weeks of chemoradiotherapy, followed by 14 maintenance doses, or placebo on the same schedule. Randomization was stratified by radiotherapy regimen, tumor site/p16 status, and disease stage (III vs IV). EFS was the primary end point of the trial, compared with OS, which was the key secondary end point, and safety was the other secondary end point. Approximately 95% of patients had detectable ctDNA at baseline regardless of HPV status or treatment arm, and baseline ctDNA levels demonstrated a moderate positive correlation with target tumor lesion size in HPV-negative (ρ = 0.494; n = 405) and HPV-positive (ρ = 0.341; n = 166) disease. Did pembrolizumab benefit patients with HPV-negative HNSCC regardless of baseline ctDNA level? In the HPV-negative subgroup, EFS and OS numerically favored pembrolizumab plus chemoradiotherapy over placebo plus chemoradiotherapy at both baseline ctDNA levels. Among patients with MSAF at or above the median in the pembrolizumab arm compared with the placebo arm, the hazard ratio (HR) for EFS was 0.75 (95% CI, 0.52-1.07) and the HR for OS was 0.85 (95% CI, 0.57-1.25). Among those with MSAF below the median, the respective HRs were 0.76 (95% CI, 0.51-1.13) and 0.73 (95% CI, 0.46-1.14). Notably, association between ctDNA clearance at cycle 3, day 1 and outcomes in HPV-negative disease was independent of ECOG performance status and other prognostic markers, including tumor size, disease stage, PD-L1 combined positive score, T-cell–inflamed gene expression profile, and tumor mutational burden. How were ctDNA levels and clearance associated with outcomes in HPV-positive HNSCC in KEYNOTE-412? In the HPV-positive subgroup, baseline ctDNA levels were not prognostic for EFS in the pembrolizumab or placebo arm, or for OS in either arm, and outcomes were similar between arms regardless of ctDNA level. ctDNA clearance at cycle 3, day 1 occurred in 81.5% of HPV-positive patients in the pembrolizumab arm (n = 65) vs 64.6% of those in the placebo arm (n = 65). In the placebo arm, patients who cleared ctDNA (n = 42) had a 5-year EFS rate of 70.2% vs 49.0% for those who did not (n = 23; P = .028). Five-year OS rates for these respective groups were of 85.5% vs 65.2% (P = .013). In the pembrolizumab arm, the 5-year EFS rates were 67.6% for patients who cleared ctDNA (n = 53) vs 41.7% for those who did not (n = 12; P = .095), and the 5-year OS rates were 78.8% vs 83.3% (P = .619). The investigators cautioned that these results should be interpreted carefully because of the small sample size. supplementary_news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Friday, October 30, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health Longer HPV Vaccine Programmes Tied to Higher Coverage Across 31 African Countries by October 29, 2026 in Health Reading Time: 5 mins read 0 Longer HPV Vaccine Programmes Tied to Higher Coverage Across 31 African Countries Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram Human papillomavirus vaccination coverage among girls in Africa has risen steadily since the vaccine first reached the continent in 2011, but it still falls well short of the World Health Organization’s target of 90 percent coverage among girls by age 15. That is the central finding of a retrospective analysis of national immunisation data from 31 African countries, published in Discover Public Health, which also reports that each additional year a country runs its HPV vaccination programme is associated with roughly a three-percentage-point increase in first-dose coverage. By 2024, only 31 of Africa’s 54 countries had integrated HPV vaccination into their routine immunisation schedules, mostly targeting girls aged 9 to 14 years. Across the 31 countries, mean first-dose coverage in 2024 was 64 percent, with a standard deviation of 25.5, while last-dose coverage averaged 55 percent, with a standard deviation of 27.3. Those figures represent a modest improvement over 2023, when first-dose coverage averaged 63 percent and last-dose coverage 50 percent. Discover more Check Symptoms African Countries View Census Data The spread between countries was enormous. Five countries exceeded 90 percent first-dose coverage in 2024: Burkina Faso and Cape Verde at 99 percent, Uganda at 95 percent, the United Republic of Tanzania at 94 percent, and Mauritius at 92 percent. Botswana also reached 93 percent for the first dose, though its last-dose coverage dropped to 34 percent. At the other end of the scale, Morocco recorded just 3 percent first-dose coverage, while Gambia and Mali each managed 15 percent, Eswatini 30 percent, and Cameroon and Togo 36 percent. Discover more Buy Maps Africa African countries Shop African Art Regional patterns varied sharply. Eastern and Southern Africa recorded first-dose and last-dose coverage of 77 percent and 61 percent respectively, West and Central Africa reached 63 percent and 60 percent, while North Africa lagged at 52 percent and 27 percent. Only two of nine countries in Central Africa had initiated vaccination, Sao Tome and Principe at 75 percent and Cameroon at 36 percent, and just three of seven North African countries had begun, with Libya and Mauritania at 51 percent first-dose coverage and Morocco far behind. The temporal trend tells a story of early rapid gains, pandemic disruption, and slow recovery. From 2011 to 2016, average first-dose coverage among vaccinating countries climbed from roughly 36 percent to 89 percent, and last-dose coverage rose from about 34 percent in 2011 to nearly 70 percent by 2017. Then came a pronounced reversal: by 2018 and 2019, first-dose coverage had fallen to around 70 percent, and last-dose coverage dropped sharply to 33 percent. The decline deepened in 2020 and 2021, when first-dose coverage fell to about 51 percent and last-dose coverage hit its lowest point at 32 percent. Only from 2022 onward did coverage begin to recover, reaching 64 percent for the first dose by 2024. The authors attribute much of that mid-period collapse to the COVID-19 pandemic. First- and last-dose coverage stood at approximately 70 percent and 33 percent in 2019 but declined to 51 percent and 29 percent in 2020 following widespread disruptions. Because school-based delivery is the primary HPV vaccination strategy in many African countries, prolonged school closures substantially reduced opportunities for vaccine delivery, while health system resources were diverted to the pandemic response. Globally, 23 countries failed to report HPV vaccination coverage data in 2021, compared with only nine in 2019, with several African countries experiencing particularly severe interruptions. To test whether programme maturity matters, the researchers fitted linear regression models relating the number of years a country had implemented HPV vaccination to its 2024 first-dose coverage. The association was statistically significant: the regression coefficient was 2.97, with a standard error of 1.32, a p-value of 0.032, and an R-squared of 0.15, meaning programme duration explained about 15 percent of the variation in coverage. Each additional year of implementation was associated with an increase of roughly three percentage points in first-dose coverage. A sensitivity analysis that removed outlier countries, excluding Cape Verde and Burkina Faso at 99 percent coverage and Morocco below 5 percent, strengthened the estimate to 3.17 percentage points per year, with a 95 percent confidence interval of 0.85 to 5.5, a p-value of 0.009, and an R-squared of 0.232. Discover more Find Vaccines Book a Checkup vaccines Vaccine vaccine The analysis of vaccination completion revealed a more nuanced picture. Using 2022 data, chosen because 21 of the 31 countries had switched to single-dose schedules in 2023, the researchers found that in the crude model first-dose coverage was not significantly associated with last-dose coverage, with a coefficient of 0.304 and a p-value of 0.070. This suggests that high vaccine initiation does not by itself guarantee completion of the schedule. However, in the model adjusted for programme duration, both predictors became significant: each one-percentage-point increase in first-dose coverage was associated with an estimated 0.32-percentage-point increase in last-dose coverage, and each additional year of programme implementation was associated with an estimated 4.19-percentage-point increase in last-dose coverage. The adjusted model explained 43.3 percent of the variability in last-dose coverage, indicating that programme maturity may support completion through stronger follow-up systems, improved logistics, and better tracking of eligible adolescents. The authors caution that programme duration alone is far from sufficient. A substantial proportion of the variation in coverage remained unexplained, pointing to the influence of delivery strategies, public awareness, vaccine confidence, school enrolment, healthcare infrastructure, financing mechanisms, healthcare worker capacity, and supply chain performance. Previous studies across Africa have identified weak health system capacity, socioeconomic inequalities, vaccine-related stigma, misinformation, concerns about fertility, inadequate health education, and the financial cost of HPV vaccines, often coupled with reliance on external donor support, as barriers to scale-up. Countries such as Rwanda, Uganda, and Tanzania have achieved notable progress through comprehensive school-based programmes, community engagement, and targeted efforts to address sociocultural barriers to acceptance. The study has limitations the authors acknowledge directly. Inconsistent reporting by some countries may have left missing or incomplete data for certain years, and differences in healthcare infrastructure and data quality between regions may affect the accuracy of coverage estimates. The analysis is also ecological, examining associations at the country level rather than following individuals, so the link between programme duration and coverage cannot be interpreted as a proven causal effect at the level of any single girl’s vaccination. Nevertheless, the findings carry practical weight. Sixteen of the 31 countries studied have transitioned to single-dose schedules, which WHO recommends for its potential to reduce delivery costs, simplify logistics, and ease vaccine supply constraints. Political commitment has grown as well, with 43 African leaders signing a declaration in July 2023 committing to vaccinate 40 percent of girls aged 15 and younger by 2025. The authors conclude that reaching the 90 percent target will require sustained investment in health systems, accelerated programme expansion, and intensified efforts against vaccine hesitancy and inequities in access, with single-dose strategies offering an important opportunity to expand first-dose coverage efficiently. D., Etuk, V., Oyedele, O., Osawe, S., Andrew, N., & Okpokoro, E. (2026). Patterns, distributions and predictors of human papillomavirus vaccination coverage among girls across 31 African countries. supplementary_news.content: News Issues Wellness Beauty Pharma KOREAN SEARCH Search Health Chosun HPV Genotypes Affect Oropharyngeal Cancer Survival, With Types 33 and 35 Showing Different Clinical Risks by Oh Sang Hun Updated 2026/10/29 09:58 Professor Cha Won-jae of the Department of Otorhinolaryngology at Bundang Seoul National University Hospital, left, and Professor Jin Si-yeon of the Department of Otorhinolaryngology at Seoul National University Hospital. Photo provided by Bundang Seoul National University Hospital. One in four patients with oropharyngeal cancer in South Korea was found to be infected with an HPV genotype other than HPV 16. In particular, patients infected with HPV 33 had a higher cervical lymph node stage, while those infected with HPV 35 had lower overall survival, highlighting the need to pay attention to clinical differences by genotype, a study found. A research team led by Professor Cha Won-jae of the Department of Otorhinolaryngology at Bundang Seoul National University Hospital, with Professor Jin Si-yeon of the Department of Otorhinolaryngology at Seoul National University Hospital as first author, announced on the 29th that it reached this conclusion after analyzing 174 patients with HPV-positive oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma whose genotypes had been identified among those treated at Bundang Seoul National University Hospital between 2003 and 2023. Oropharyngeal cancer is cancer that develops in the oropharynx, the area at the back of the throat, with tonsil cancer and base-of-tongue cancer among its representative forms. Smoking and alcohol consumption were previously considered the main causes, but oropharyngeal cancer caused by HPV infection has increased in recent years. HPV is a virus transmitted through direct contact with the skin or mucous membranes, and some high-risk genotypes can cause cancer if the infection persists. HPV 16 is the most commonly detected genotype in HPV-positive oropharyngeal cancer, so previous studies have focused mainly on type 16. However, when the research team analyzed the HPV genotypes of patients in South Korea, it found that 25.3% of all patients, 44 people, were infected with a genotype other than type 16. By genotype, type 16 was the most common at 74.7%, followed by type 33 at 6.3%, type 35 at 4.6%, and types 58 and 18 at 3.4% each. Differences in clinical characteristics and prognosis were also observed according to genotype. Patients infected with HPV 33 had a higher lymph node stage, indicating the extent of cervical lymph node metastasis at diagnosis, than patients infected with HPV 16. Patients infected with HPV 35 had lower overall survival than those infected with HPV 16. The research team explained that the existing perception that HPV-positive oropharyngeal cancer has a better prognosis than HPV-negative oropharyngeal cancer is also based largely on studies focused on type 16, making it necessary to examine the clinical characteristics and prognosis of other genotypes in greater detail. In this study, 90.8% of all patients, 158 people, were men. The male predominance was common across all genotypes. The findings demonstrate the need to prevent HPV infection and related diseases in men as well. Professor Jin Si-yeon said, “In addition to HPV 16, various high-risk genotypes, including type 33, were identified at levels that cannot be ignored. If the four-valent HPV vaccine currently used in the National Immunization Program is switched to the nine-valent vaccine, we expect the range of prevention to be expanded further.” The four-valent HPV vaccine currently prevents types 6, 11, 16, and 18, while the nine-valent vaccine additionally covers types 31, 33, 45, 52, and 58. Professor Cha Won-jae said, “As surgical techniques, radiation and chemotherapy, and multidisciplinary approaches have advanced in recent years, HPV-positive oropharyngeal cancer has generally shown favorable treatment outcomes. We hope this study will help develop a more detailed understanding of the clinical characteristics and prognostic differences according to HPV genotype.” The study was published in Clinical and Experimental Otorhinolaryngology, an international academic journal in the field of otorhinolaryngology. supplementary_news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Friday, October 30, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health Saudi parent survey finds high childhood vaccination but uneven HPV awareness by October 26, 2026 in Health Reading Time: 3 mins read 0 Saudi parent survey finds high childhood vaccination but uneven HPV awareness Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram A cross-sectional online survey of 513 parents in Saudi Arabia found high self-reported childhood vaccination coverage but less uniform awareness of and willingness to recommend human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination. Overall, 98.8% of respondents said their children had received routine vaccinations, and 90.6% reported completing the recommended vaccinations. General vaccine awareness was reported by 96.9%, while awareness of national immunization programs was reported by 57.9%. Among the parents surveyed, 68.6% said they were aware of the HPV vaccine, 52.4% said they would recommend HPV vaccination for their child, and 19.1% selected “I don’t know” when asked about making a recommendation. Researchers conducted the survey from June to July 2025 using an Arabic questionnaire adapted to examine vaccination awareness and perceptions, sources of vaccination information, parent-reported vaccination practices and experiences, and awareness of national immunization programs. Two HPV-specific questions assessed awareness of the vaccine and recommendation intention. The investigators used descriptive analyses, chi-square tests and Fisher’s exact tests for group comparisons. They also fitted a multivariable binary logistic regression to examine factors associated with HPV vaccine awareness and an exploratory multinomial logistic regression to compare different recommendation intentions. Because the study was observational, cross-sectional and based on self-reports through an online questionnaire, it describes reported attitudes and behaviors rather than independently verified vaccination records, and its associations cannot establish that any measured factor caused awareness or recommendation intention. Discover more Book a Checkup Find Vaccines Find Family Lawyer child children Health workers were the most frequently selected source of vaccination information, selected by 60.0% of respondents. The survey also found that 61.4% of parents reported being satisfied with vaccination information in the media. The source questions concerned vaccination information generally and did not separately establish which sources parents used for HPV vaccination. The data therefore do not support treating the health-worker finding as a direct measure of HPV information-seeking or as evidence about the adequacy of public coverage. Adjusted analysis found several characteristics associated with HPV vaccine awareness. Female respondents had higher odds of reporting awareness than male respondents, with an adjusted odds ratio of 1.87 and a 95% confidence interval of 1.23–2.86. Parents in every other region included in the analysis had higher adjusted odds of awareness than parents in the Southern region, with adjusted odds ratios ranging from 2.02 to 3.38 across the regional comparisons. These are cross-sectional geographic associations, not evidence of a decline or improvement over time. Parents who reported problems during vaccination also had higher adjusted odds of HPV awareness, with an adjusted odds ratio of 2.82 and a 95% confidence interval of 1.76–4.51. Parents who expressed either a harmful or non-harmful view of vaccination also had higher adjusted odds of awareness than those who answered “I don’t know” to the general vaccination-view question. In the exploratory multinomial model, HPV vaccine awareness was associated with a lower relative likelihood of answering “I don’t know” rather than “Yes” when asked whether respondents would recommend HPV vaccination for their child. The adjusted relative risk ratio was 0.07, with a 95% confidence interval of 0.04–0.13. Discover more Hire Babysitters vaccine Health Get Health Tips health The estimate indicates a strong statistical association in this sample, but it does not show that HPV awareness caused parents to recommend vaccination. Taken together, the results portray a population in which routine childhood immunization was widely reported, while HPV awareness and recommendation intention were less consistent and included a sizable undecided group. The authors concluded that the findings support stronger provider communication and credible public messaging, particularly for lower-awareness regions and uncertain parents. The study’s online, self-reported, cross-sectional design and the limited number of HPV-specific questions mean that the results should be interpreted as a snapshot of this surveyed population rather than a causal evaluation of vaccine communication or a measure of vaccination coverage across all Saudi parents. 7种高危致癌型HPV抗体水平显著高于进口九价疫苗 希腊雅典2026年10月28日 /美通社/ -- 近日,在希腊雅典举行的第38届国际乳头瘤病毒学会学术大会(IPVS 2026)上,国际知名全球公共卫生组织——美国帕斯适宜卫生科技组织(Program on Appropriate Technology of Health,PATH)公布了一项评估九价HPV疫苗单剂接种程序国际III期多中心临床研究的第6个月中期分析结果。数据显示,9-20岁年轻女性接种单剂次国产万泰九价HPV疫苗馨可宁®9后,针对7种高危致癌HPV型别的IgG抗体几何平均浓度(GMC)均显著高于默沙东佳达修®9,且安全性表现总体相近。 7种高危HPV型别免疫应答均高于对照疫苗 加纳纳夫隆戈卫生研究中心(Navrongo Health Research Centre,NHRC)临床科学部主任Nana Akosua Ansah博士是该项研究的主要研究者,她在大会期间公布了由国际知名全球公共卫生组织PATH发起、盖茨基金会资助的新型HPV疫苗单剂次免疫桥接研究(Single-dose HPV Immunobridging Study with New Vaccines I,简称SHINE I;研究编号CVIA 104)第6个月中期分析结果。 该研究是一项在加纳和菲律宾开展的国际多中心、随机、双盲III期临床试验,共纳入1,320名9—20岁女性试验参与者,旨在比较单剂接种国产九价HPV疫苗馨可宁®9与默沙东佳达修®9的免疫原性和安全性。 Nana Akosua Ansah博士公布:单剂接种后第6个月,馨可宁®9针对全部9种HPV型别(6、11、16、18、31、33、45、52、58)的IgG抗体血清阳转率高达95.7%—100%。 针对HPV 16、18、31、33、45、52和58全部7种高危致癌型别,馨可宁®9在9-14岁以及15-20岁两个年龄队列中的IgG抗体GMC在数值上均高于佳达修®9,GMC比值范围为1.38—2.54,所有比值的95%置信区间下限均大于1.0。 对于另外两种非致癌型别,馨可宁®9针对HPV 6的IgG抗体水平在两个队列中同样高于对照疫苗;针对HPV 11的抗体水平略低于对照疫苗,但95%置信区间存在重叠,下限仍满足非劣效。 图片来源:IPVS 2026大会PATH主导的SHINE I研究第6个月中期数据报告现场。 安全性总体相近,研究将继续开展 安全性方面,截至接种后第6个月,两个疫苗组相应年龄队列中的不良事件发生率总体相近,均未出现与疫苗接种相关的严重不良反应,未发现新的安全性信号。 图片来源:IPVS 2026大会PATH主导的SHINE I研究第6个月中期数据报告现场。 万泰九价HPV疫苗馨可宁®9助力全球消除宫颈癌目标 随着全球HPV疫苗单剂接种策略持续推进,如何以更简化的接种程序、更可负担的成本扩大疫苗覆盖,已成为加速消除宫颈癌的重要课题。此次国际多中心研究公布的中期数据,不仅为国产九价HPV疫苗单剂接种的免疫原性和安全性提供了新的临床证据,也展现了中国创新疫苗参与全球公共卫生实践的潜力。未来,随着国产九价 HPV 疫苗更多应用场景下临床数据的积累,将为优化全球HPV疫苗免疫策略、提升中低收入国家疫苗可及性提供科学支持,为实现世界卫生组织提出的全球消除宫颈癌目标贡献不可或缺的新力量。 注:本次公布的是单剂接种后第6个月中期分析结果,研究将进一步考察24个月的免疫原性非劣效临床终点结果。 The quadrivalent human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine demonstrates sustained immunogenicity and low rates of HPV-related infection and disease among women with HIV during up to 9 years of follow-up. Continued HIV viral suppression is also associated with a reduced risk for HPV antibody seroreversion. These study findings were published in The Lancet HIV. Women with HIV are at increased risk for HPV infection and associated cervical disease compared with women without HIV. Although previous studies have demonstrated strong initial immune responses to HPV vaccination in this population, data on long-term immunogenicity and clinical outcomes remain limited. Researchers evaluated antibody responses and HPV-related outcomes following quadrivalent HPV vaccination among women with HIV. In this longitudinal cohort study, the researchers recruited girls andSTI women with HIV from 14 HIV and gynecologic care clinics across Canada. The current analysis included participants aged 16 years and older who received the quadrivalent HPV vaccine targeting HPV types 6, 11, 16, and 18. Participants were offered 3 vaccine doses at months 0, 2, and 6, with follow-up conducted from July 2008 through June 2019. Clinical characteristics, HPV antibody levels, cervical cytology, and HPV DNA genotyping were assessed at baseline and at follow-up visits every 6 to 12 months. Immunogenicity outcomes included antibody geometric mean titers (GMTs), seropositivity, and seroreversion. Clinical outcomes included persistent vaccine-type HPV infection, genital warts, and cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 2 or higher (CIN2+). Continued engagement in HIV care to maintain HIV viral load suppression is important in maintaining anti-HPV antibody titres to ensure long-term protection. A total of 353 participants received at least 1 vaccine dose, including 293 in the adult intention-to-treat population and 228 in the per-protocol population. The per-protocol analysis included participants who completed all 3 vaccine doses within 1 year and had no evidence of prior infection with the relevant HPV type at baseline. Among participants in the per-protocol population, the median age was 38.5 (IQR, 32.0-45.4) years, and the median CD4+ count was 499.5 (IQR, 380.8-700.0) cells/μL. At baseline, 160 (70.2%) participants had suppressed HIV viral loads (<50 copies/mL). The population included participants who identified as African, Caribbean, or Black (43.9%), White (36.8%), or Indigenous (11.0%). The median follow-up duration was 5.9 (IQR, 2.3-7.7) years. At month 7, seroconversion rates were 99% for HPV6, 99% for HPV11, 98% for HPV16, and 94% for HPV18. Antibody GMTs initially decreased following the peak response but subsequently stabilized, with sustained antibody responses observed through 9 years. Among women aged 24 to 45 years, antibody GMTs were generally comparable to those reported in a historical cohort of women without HIV. Peak antibody levels were similar between groups for HPV6, HPV11, and HPV18, while peak HPV16 titers were higher among women without HIV. During subsequent follow-up, HPV16 titers were comparable between groups, whereas titers for several other HPV types were higher among women with HIV. In the per-protocol population, seroreversion occurred in 18 of 132 (13.6%) participants for HPV6, 22 of 186 (11.8%) for HPV11, 12 of 141 (8.5%) for HPV16, and 60 of 165 (36.4%) for HPV18. After adjustment for age at vaccination and peak antibody titers, HIV viral suppression during follow-up was associated with a lower risk for seroreversion for HPV16 (hazard ratio [HR], 0.06; 95% CI, 0.01-0.35; P =.0016) and HPV18 (HR, 0.32; 95% CI, 0.18-0.59; P =.0002). Higher peak antibody titers were also associated with reduced seroreversion risk across all 4 HPV types (all P <.0001), while CD4+ counts measured over time were not significant predictors. In the intention-to-treat population, HIV viral suppression was associated with a lower risk for seroreversion across all 4 HPV types, with HRs ranging from 0.10 for HPV16 to 0.64 for HPV18. The incidence of persistent vaccine-type HPV infection was 0.52 (95% CI, 0.22-1.10) per 100 person-years in the per-protocol population, with 6 cases identified during 1151.6 person-years of follow-up. Of these infections, 4 involved HPV18, 1 involved HPV16, and 1 involved HPV6. Participants who developed persistent HPV infection had lower median baseline CD4+ counts than the overall per-protocol population (350.0 vs 510.0 cells/μL). Median CD4+ nadirs were also lower among participants with persistent infection (107.0 vs 230.0 cells/μL). Among participants in the per-protocol population, 4 cases of genital warts occurred during 1089.5 person-years, corresponding to an incidence rate of 0.37 (95% CI, 0.12-0.87) per 100 person-years. No cases of CIN2+ were reported among participants with normal baseline cervical cytology during 1024.5 person-years of follow-up (incidence rate, 0.00; 95% CI, 0.00-0.24 per 100 person-years). In the intention-to-treat population, incidence rates (per 100 person-years) were 1.26 (95% CI, 0.77-1.94) for persistent HPV infection and 1.50 (95% CI, 0.95-2.28) for genital warts. One case of CIN2+ occurred, although HPV16 infection had been documented before vaccination. Comparisons with historical data from women without HIV showed similar CIN2+ incidence rates between groups. However, genital wart incidence was higher among women with HIV in the intention-to-treat and baseline HPV type-naive populations. Study limitations include the small number of persistent HPV infections and cervical disease events, which restricted analyses of associated risk factors. The absence of a placebo-controlled comparison group required the use of historical cohorts, and loss to follow-up may have introduced bias. “Continued engagement in HIV care to maintain HIV viral load suppression is important in maintaining anti-HPV antibody titres to ensure long-term protection,” the researchers concluded. Multiple study authors declared affiliations with biotech, pharmaceutical, and/or device companies. Please see the original reference for a full list of disclosures. ISRG -3.73% OPK 0.00% Waters WAT recently announced a partnership with Labcorp Holdings Inc. LH to expand access to the FDA-approved BD Onclarity HPV Assay through Labcorp's nationwide laboratory network, beginning in late 2026. The collaboration aims to broaden cervical cancer screening options by making the test available through clinician-collected and self-collected samples in clinics, patient service centers and at-home settings. Waters' management highlighted that the partnership could help address barriers to cervical cancer screening, including privacy, access and socioeconomic factors. The collaboration aims to expand access through more flexible screening options and personalized risk assessment to reach underserved populations and close existing gaps in preventive care. WAT Stock Trend Following the News WAT stock has inched up 0.5% since the announcement on Friday. Year to date, the stock has gained 20.1%, outperforming the industry's 1% decline and the S&P 500's 11.3% rise. The partnership could support WAT's growth by expanding the commercial reach of its advanced diagnostics portfolio through Labcorp's extensive healthcare network. Wider access to the BD Onclarity HPV Assay may encourage greater adoption of its testing technology among healthcare providers and patients seeking convenient screening options. The collaboration could also strengthen Waters' position in molecular diagnostics by connecting its testing capabilities with established laboratory and consumer healthcare channels, creating opportunities to increase demand as screening programs expand. WAT currently has a market capitalization of $44.57 billion. Zacks Investment Research Image Source: Zacks Investment Research More on the News The BD Onclarity HPV Assay is the only FDA-approved HPV test that supports all American Society for Colposcopy and Cervical Pathology (ASCCP) Enduring Risk-Based Management Guidelines through comprehensive extended genotyping. It individually identifies six high-risk HPV types — 16, 18, 31, 45, 51 and 52 — alongside three groups of pooled results, providing detailed information to help guide patient management. Under the partnership, Labcorp intends to offer the assay through its network, which serves more than 850,000 physicians and healthcare providers and over 2,200 patient service centers. Testing will be available through clinician programs, health plan Gaps in Care initiatives and Labcorp OnDemand, its consumer-facing testing channel. The combination of clinician-collected and self-collected screening options is intended to make testing more accessible to women who may otherwise delay or miss recommended screening. Story Continues The collaboration comes as cervical cancer screening remains an important preventive healthcare need, with many women overdue for recommended testing. High-risk HPV genotypes are associated with cervical cancer, making detailed genotype information valuable for assessing risk and guiding follow-up care. Waters and Labcorp intend to make the BD Onclarity HPV Assay available through the expanded offering by the end of 2026. The partnership could broaden the reach of Waters' diagnostics technology, with its eventual commercial impact depending on test adoption and utilization across Labcorp's network. Industry Prospects Favoring the Market According to Grand View Research, the global human papillomavirus (HPV) testing market is estimated to be valued at $2.2 billion in 2026 and is expected to witness a CAGR of 14.4% through 2033. Factors such as the rising prevalence of HPV-related cancers, growing awareness of cervical cancer screening, increasing adoption of advanced molecular diagnostic technologies and expanding access to self-collection testing options are expected to drive market growth. Other News Waters recently partnered with Quest Diagnostics to expand nationwide access to the FDA-cleared Onclarity Self-Collection Kit for at-home HPV screening. Beginning in 2027, Quest Diagnostics will offer the option through clinician, health plan, consumer health and patient service center channels, helping address barriers to cervical cancer screening. Waters also launched AI Link, integrating Anthropic's Model Context Protocol into its waters_connect software to enable AI-driven laboratory workflows. The technology allows scientists to control instruments using AI agents, automate experiments and accelerate research and development, with workflows extending into regulated environments. supplementary_news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Friday, October 30, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health Parents’ HPV vaccine choices hinge on protection duration and social cues by October 28, 2026 in Health Reading Time: 2 mins read 0 Parents' HPV vaccine choices hinge on protection duration and social cues Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram Parental hesitancy remains a major barrier to human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination, and a new discrete choice experiment published in Archives of Public Health offers a detailed look at what actually drives parents’ decisions. The study, made available online as an open-access research article on 28 October 2026, combined a stated-preference survey with an intertemporal choice task to quantify how parents weigh vaccine attributes, how steeply they discount future benefits, and how social signals shape their willingness to vaccinate. In the experiment, protection duration and vaccine effectiveness emerged as the primary determinants of parental choice. Parents also valued social-reference information: they were more likely to choose vaccination when told that healthcare professionals’ own children had been vaccinated. Notably, the vaccine’s origin showed no significant effect on choices. The researchers estimated attribute preferences using a mixed logit model and used latent class analysis to identify heterogeneity, segmenting the cohort into a receptive majority of 79.4 percent and a hesitant minority of 20.6 percent. The study also probed intertemporal preferences by measuring monetary discount rates, a proxy for how strongly people favor immediate over delayed rewards. Interaction models indicated that monetary discounting was jointly associated with the structure of parents’ preferences. However, the authors report that no individual attribute interaction survived adjustment for multiple testing, meaning those attribute-level findings should be treated as exploratory. Interestingly, higher monetary discount rates were associated with membership in the receptive majority rather than the hesitant group. Discover more Find Vaccines vaccine Book a Checkup Read Med Journals Read Bestsellers The authors conclude that parental decisions about HPV vaccination reflect a combination of clinical attributes, social reference information and intertemporal preferences. Because protection duration and vaccine effectiveness mattered most, and because social-reference information about healthcare professionals’ children appeared to encourage vaccine uptake, they suggest that reducing out-of-pocket costs and communicating credible social-reference information are strategies worth testing in future intervention research. Given that the sample was predominantly urban and highly educated, the findings should be generalized with caution. The findings identify the microbiome as a promising biological correlate of treatment response, but the authors caution that the direct post-treatment evidence remains limited to five studies and does not yet support clinical testing or microbiome-based therapy. Persistent high-risk HPV is the necessary cause of virtually all HSIL and cervical cancer, yet most infections do not produce disease. Approximately 70% to 90% of new high-risk HPV infections clear spontaneously within one or two years, while only a minority progress. The review places this apparent mismatch between viral exposure and clinical outcome in the context of the cervicovaginal microbiome, a community of bacteria and, to a lesser extent, fungi and viruses inhabiting the vaginal and ectocervical mucosa. This microbial ecosystem may influence HPV persistence through changes in acidity, barrier integrity, inflammation, metabolite signaling and local immunity, although many of the proposed causal pathways remain experimental. Research led by Ravel and colleagues established that reproductive-age vaginal communities often fall into five principal community state types. Four are dominated by a single Lactobacillus species: CST-I by L. crispatus, CST-II by L. gasseri, CST-III by L. iners and CST-V by L. jensenii. CST-IV instead contains a diverse, largely anaerobic mixture with depleted Lactobacillus and is associated with bacterial vaginosis. These states are dynamic rather than fixed, shifting over days or weeks in response to factors including menstruation, sexual activity and hygiene. Menopause can also alter the community: declining estrogen reduces glycogen available to support Lactobacillus proliferation, while CST-IV-like and more diverse states become more common in some populations. Discover more Study Anatomy Track Fertility Find an OBGYN Study Biology See an OB-GYN Across observational studies, women with persistent high-risk HPV or more advanced cervical lesions generally carried higher microbial diversity and less Lactobacillus than women who cleared the virus or had no HPV. In an Italian cohort followed for one year, CST-IV was present in 43% of women whose infection persisted, compared with 7.4% of those who cleared it, while Atopobium species were enriched in the persistence group. Another cohort found that decreasing lactobacilli was independently associated with HPV persistence after adjustment for age and menopausal status. Findings from bacterial-vaginosis studies also connected dysbiosis with higher viral persistence and cytological progression. These observations establish an association, but they do not show that microbiome composition itself causes HPV to persist. Laboratory experiments offer possible explanations for the pattern. In cultures of HPV16-transformed cervical cells, L. crispatus and L. gasseri reduced expression of the viral E6 and E7 oncoproteins and downstream p53 and Rb pathways, whereas some dysbiosis-associated bacteria produced contrasting effects. A cocktail containing L. crispatus, L. gasseri and L. jensenii also lowered E6, E7, cyclin A and CDK2 expression in vitro. L. crispatus is distinguished by producing D-lactic acid, which can lower vaginal pH and stimulate anti-inflammatory epithelial responses. Other experiments linked lactic acid to miR-744, a microRNA associated with suppression of E6 and E7 through direct and ARHGAP5-mediated pathways. Dysbiotic metabolite profiles, meanwhile, have been associated with increased TNF-alpha and reduced protective chemokines such as RANTES and IP-10. Proposed effects on cervical Langerhans cells, the antigen-presenting cells that help direct HPV-specific immunity, add another possible pathway, but these molecular results have not yet been confirmed as mechanisms operating in treated patients. Discover more Book a Checkup Find Cancer Care Read Horoscopes The most directly relevant studies concern women undergoing loop electrosurgical excision procedure, or LEEP, or conization for HSIL. Excision removes the HPV-associated lesion but also physically remodels the cervicovaginal niche. In a prospective Italian study of 41 women, four patients who developed persistent infection or CIN2/3 recurrence within six months had nominally L. crispatus-dominated baseline communities but carried unusually high loads of Gardnerella vaginalis, Ureaplasma parvum and Candida albicans. This suggests that co-colonization may distinguish women at risk of failure within an apparently favorable community. A separate Chinese cohort of 26 patients found that microbial diversity fell after LEEP and that pretreatment Lactobacillus depletion was associated with persistent HPV at three months. In 108 women studied around conization, persistent HPV was associated not only with bacterial-vaginosis anaerobes such as Gardnerella and Atopobium but also with Enterococcus and related aerobic-vaginitis organisms, as well as anaerobic and biofilm-forming phenotypes. Perhaps the clearest sign that treatment response and microbiome change are connected came from 85 HSIL patients whose vaginal communities were assessed before and after conization. CST-IV prevalence fell significantly among women who subsequently cleared high-risk HPV, but remained essentially unchanged among those with persistent infection. A Norwegian cohort of 89 LEEP patients and 100 cytologically normal references likewise documented post-treatment shifts and explored whether cone depth influenced associations between microbiota and HPV persistence. Taken together, the direct evidence supports three linked observations: pretreatment dysbiosis is associated with poorer outcomes, excision alters the microbial community, and movement toward Lactobacillus dominance after the operation tracks with viral clearance. The last pattern may be a marker of successful recovery, a contributor to clearance, or both; the available studies cannot distinguish those possibilities. Machine-learning models offer another route to prediction, but none has yet been trained and validated specifically for post-treatment clearance. A study of 272 women identified taxa including Stenotrophomonas, Streptococcus and Pseudomonas as more abundant in HSIL, while Dialister, Bifidobacterium, Faecalibacterium and Bacteroides were depleted, and proposed abundance thresholds as potential screening adjuncts. A separate random-forest classifier built from 33 species separated CIN2 or worse from CIN1 or lower with an area under the curve of 0.952, identifying L. iners as its strongest contributor. Multi-omics work has also suggested that the cervicovaginal metabolome may predict the local microenvironment more effectively than microbial composition alone. These models classify lesion presence or severity, however, rather than viral clearance after LEEP or conization, leaving a major translational gap. Probiotic trials suggest that microbiome-directed treatment might affect HPV outcomes, although the evidence is inconsistent and remains distinct from HSIL treatment studies. In a controlled pilot of 54 women with HPV-associated cytological abnormalities, an oral probiotic drink produced numerically higher HPV clearance than no intervention, 29% versus 19%, although the difference was not statistically significant; clearance of cytological abnormalities reached 60% versus 31%, with p=0.05. A randomized, double-blind trial of oral L. rhamnosus GR-1 and L. reuteri RC-14 in 121 women found no significant difference in HPV clearance, 58.1% with probiotic and 54.2% with placebo, though smear quality improved. Direct intravaginal delivery has looked more favorable: a prospective controlled pilot of L. crispatus chen-01 in 100 women reported lower viral load, higher clearance and improved vaginal inflammation, with sequencing indicating reconstitution of Lactobacillus dominance. Nevertheless, strain, dose, delivery and outcome definitions varied substantially among trials, and no randomized trial reviewed specifically tested a microbiome intervention alongside LEEP or conization. The review’s confidence is further limited by small cohorts, generally 26 to 108 participants in direct peri-treatment studies; inconsistent profiling methods, including microscopy, targeted assays, 16S sequencing and metagenomics; follow-up of only three to 12 months; and limited adjustment for sexual activity, antibiotic use, contraception, smoking and HIV status. Community-state distributions also vary across populations, limiting generalization from any single country or ethnic group. The authors did not pool effect estimates or perform formal risk-of-bias weighting, and their search excluded non-English studies, potentially missing relevant Chinese-language research on post-treatment microbiomes. Future priorities include adequately powered, multiethnic cohorts sampling women before and repeatedly after excision; standardized sequencing and outcome definitions; externally validated prediction models built with post-treatment endpoints; trials of intravaginal L. crispatus as an adjunct to HSIL therapy; and mechanistic studies that directly connect microbial, immune and viral measurements within the treatment window. Until then, the microbiome is a compelling correlate and experimental target, not a clinically validated predictor or therapy. Of the participants, 30.7% reported receiving the HPV vaccine, while 19.0% had completed the two-dose schedule. The most commonly reported barriers were lack of awareness, fear of side effects and limited access to vaccination services. The researchers recruited participants through multistage sampling between August and October 2025. They gathered quantitative data with a semi-structured questionnaire, analyzed the results using descriptive statistics and logistic regression in Stata 16.0, and examined focus group discussions through thematic analysis. The participants had a mean age of 19.76 years, with a standard deviation of 3.00 years. The design captured vaccination status and reported experiences at one point in time, so it can identify associations but cannot establish that particular factors caused low uptake or completion. Discover more Check Symptoms Health health Qualitative findings indicated that knowledge gaps and misconceptions about HPV and vaccination were among the reported obstacles. Parental influence on vaccination decisions also featured prominently in the focus group discussions. Participants described health-system barriers including poor communication, inconsistent availability of vaccination services and negative healthcare experiences. Distance to vaccination sites and limited transport options created additional structural constraints for some residents. These findings explain reported experiences within the study population; they do not establish the prevalence of each barrier across all young women in Kampala’s urban slums. Discover more Find Vaccines Book a Checkup Support Causes Find Housing Two factors were associated with lower adjusted odds of remaining unvaccinated. Participants who lived near a vaccination clinic had an adjusted odds ratio of 0.35 for being unvaccinated, with a 95% confidence interval of 0.21–0.60, compared with participants who did not have that proximity. Those who reported receiving counselling from a healthcare worker also had lower adjusted odds of remaining unvaccinated, with an adjusted odds ratio of 0.19 and a 95% confidence interval of 0.11–0.34. These are adjusted statistical associations rather than evidence that clinic proximity or counselling alone caused vaccination or completion. The study did not test a vaccination intervention or demonstrate that any proposed strategy had increased coverage in Kampala. Its authors identified community sensitisation, improved healthcare-worker communication and expanded community- and school-based delivery as possible approaches to improving equitable access, while stating that further research would be needed to assess their effectiveness in this setting. The results are also limited to the sampled urban-slum areas and to adolescent girls and young women aged 15–24 years, meaning they should not automatically be applied to other age groups, locations or HPV vaccination programs. supplementary_news.content: Clinical Hub News & Perspective Tools & Reference CME/CE More EN RegisterLog In Ask AI Search AI Mode Medscape Europe A Single Case of Durable Nivolumab Response in Oropharyngeal Cancer Wolfgang Paik October 26, 2026 0 2 Add to Email Alerts Jump to Key Points Key Takeaways The case involved a human papillomavirus-positive (HPV-positive) squamous cell carcinoma of the oropharynx, staged cT2N2bM0. The patient underwent extensive treatment, including bilateral neck dissection, and later received nivolumab, which resulted in a durable response within 2 months. Despite treatment being stopped because of an adverse skin reaction, the response has been maintained for 4 years. The case report by oncologist Maria Abreu, MD, and colleagues from the Unidade Local de Saúde Lisboa Ocidental in Lisbon, Portugal, documents the potential for a sustained complete response even after discontinuation of immunotherapy. The Patient and Her Medical History A 69-year-old woman presented to a hospital in Lisbon, Portugal, with a sensation of a foreign body in the hypopharynx that had persisted for 10 days. She denied dysphagia, dysphonia, dyspnea, or odynophagia. A history of duodenal ulcer was known. Her regular medications included omeprazole, simvastatin, amlodipine, and valsartan. The family, social, substance use, travel, and allergy histories were unremarkable. SUGGESTED FOR YOU Findings Upon admission, the patient’s vital signs were measured. Respiratory rate, heart rate, blood pressure, oxygen saturation on room air, and body temperature were within their respective normal ranges. Inspection, auscultation, palpation, and percussion of the patient’s body confirmed the information provided in the medical history. A hypertrophic lesion was noted on the left base of the tongue, which was firmly palpable using both hands. Bilateral laterocervical lymphadenopathy was present, with a predominance on the left (particularly at level III). Indirect videolaryngoscopy revealed a lesion affecting the left half of the base of the tongue and the vallecula but sparing the tonsils and lateral pharyngeal walls. MRI confirmed the presence of an oval, primarily exophytic mass in the left base of the tongue measuring 31 × 23 × 22.5 mm, extending inferiorly to the vallecula. The ipsilateral glossoepiglottic fold and the posterior pharyngeal wall were not involved. On the left side, at levels II and III, a cluster of four lymph nodes with a combined short-axis diameter of approximately 5 cm was identified. Following biopsy and histopathologic evaluation, an HPV-positive squamous cell carcinoma was diagnosed. The tumor board classified the tumor as cT2N2bM0. Treatment Induction therapy was followed by chemoradiotherapy. However, posttreatment MRI revealed persistent disease, necessitating extensive surgery, including partial pharyngectomy with tracheostomy, hemiglossectomy, and microvascular flap reconstruction. A bilateral neck dissection was also performed. Systemic therapy with paclitaxel was subsequently initiated. The patient did not tolerate the medication well, so she was switched to cetuximab and methotrexate. Nevertheless, a CT scan performed as part of follow-up care revealed a locoregional recurrence. Hemostatic palliative radiotherapy was initiated. Following immunohistochemical analysis, therapy with nivolumab was started. While on nivolumab, the patient achieved a complete response within 2 months. However, 1 month later, she developed a generalized, difficult-to-treat, itchy rash, necessitating discontinuation of therapy. Surprisingly, follow-up examinations over the past 4 years have shown that the complete response to therapy has been maintained. Discussion “We report a case of durable CR [complete response] in a heavily pretreated HPV-positive oropharyngeal carcinoma, maintained for more than 4 years after nivolumab discontinuation,” wrote the authors of the case report. The case underscores the potential for long-term remission through immunotherapy even in an unfavorable clinical setting. Furthermore, it raises questions regarding the optimal duration of treatment, patient selection, and the potential role of immune-mediated drug side effects as prognostic markers. This story was translated from Univadis Germany, part of the Medscape Professional Network.
